contributions.text_english: Thank you, Llywydd. There is one change to this week's business. The debate on the legislative consent motion on the Armed Forces Bill has been extended to half an hour, in recognition of the interest shown by Members. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available, as usual, to all Members electronically.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Lywydd. Mae yna un newid i fusnes yr wythnos hon. Mae'r ddadl ar y cynnig cydsyniad deddfwriaethol ar Fil y Lluoedd Arfog wedi ymestyn i hanner awr, i gydnabod y diddordeb a ddangoswyd gan yr Aelodau. Mae busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael, fel arfer, i'r holl Aelodau yn electronig.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you. On the first point, you will be aware that those processes will be followed in relation to the budget, and there will be an opportunity for everyone to express their view on the supplementary budget once again. Nothing has been broken in terms of the ministerial code in terms of what happened today; this is how Parliaments work. If Reform were a party that is serious about the future of this Senedd, and wanted to seriously discuss getting the best settlement for the people of Wales, you'd understand how parties collaborate in this Chamber and beyond.

In terms of AI, it's hugely important that we are alive to the advantages and risks related to AI, and I know that this is an issue that the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy does take as an issue of great importance. There will be updates, and, as you know, the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy is taking questions in this Senedd next week.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch. O ran y pwynt cyntaf, mi fyddwch chi’n ymwybodol bydd y prosesau yna yn cael eu dilyn o ran y gyllideb, ac mi fydd yna gyfle i bawb i fod yn rhoi barn ar y gyllideb atodol unwaith eto. Does yna ddim byd wedi’i dorri o ran y cod gweinidogol o ran yr hyn ddigwyddodd heddiw; fel hyn mae Seneddau yn gweithio. Ac, efallai, pe byddai Reform yn blaid sydd o ddifrif ynglŷn â dyfodol y Senedd hon, ac eisiau trafod o ddifrif a chael y setliad gorau i bobl Cymru, fe fyddech chi’n deall sut mae pleidiau yn cydweithio yn y Siambr hon a thu hwnt.

O ran AI, mae’n bwysig iawn ein bod ni yn fyw i’r manteision a’r risgiau sydd yn gysylltiedig ag AI, a dwi’n gwybod bod hwn yn fater y mae’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni yn ei gymryd fel mater sydd o bwys mawr. Mi fydd yna ddiweddariadau, ac, fel y byddwch chi’n gwybod, mae’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni yn derbyn cwestiynau yn y Senedd hon yr wythnos nesaf.

contributions.text_english: Thank you. I will certainly make the Cabinet Minister aware that you've raised this issue. Of course, the Cabinet Minister for Finance is present here, and you'll be aware of some of the steps that have already been taken by this Government to support businesses. Obviously, if there are any specific businesses that you are concerned about, then it's always important that Members do raise these concerns with the Ministers, but I will certainly make him aware of what you've raised.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. Mi wnaf i yn sicr wneud y Gweinidog Cabinet yn ymwybodol eich bod chi wedi codi’r mater hwn. Wrth gwrs, mae Gweinidog y Cabinet dros Gyllid yma, ac mi fyddwch chi’n ymwybodol o rai camau sydd wedi’u cymryd gan y Llywodraeth hon eisoes i gefnogi busnesau. Yn amlwg, os oes yna fusnesau penodol rydych chi’n pryderu amdanyn nhw, mae wastad yn bwysig bod Aelodau yn codi’r pryderon hyn gyda’r Gweinidogion, ond mi fyddaf i'n sicr yn ei wneud o’n ymwybodol o’r hyn rydych chi wedi’i godi.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I don't know, from what you've outlined, if you have written to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning; clearly, she is in the Chamber and will have heard your comments. You will also be aware that there are formal processes to be followed in relation to any concerns, including with the ombudsman, if concerns have been expressed. I hope that the Member will raise these concerns through those appropriate channels, so that what has been set out can be looked into if there are concerns.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Dwi ddim yn gwybod, o'r hyn roeddech chi'n ei amlinellu, a ydych chi wedi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio; yn amlwg, mae hi yn y Siambr ac wedi clywed hyn. Mi fyddwch chi hefyd yn ymwybodol bod yna brosesau ffurfiol i'w dilyn ynglŷn ag unrhyw bryderon, gan gynnwys gyda'r ombwdsmon, os oes yna bryderon wedi eu mynegi. Dwi'n gobeithio bod yr Aelod yn codi'r pryderon hyn drwy'r ffyrdd priodol hynny, fel bod yr hyn sydd wedi ei nodi yn cael ei ymchwilio iddo fo os oes yna bryderon.

contributions.text_english: Certainly. You will have heard the Cabinet Minister talking about the advantages, but also the risks, of AI, and, certainly, there is a recognition, in terms of a number of sectors, when it comes to those risks to jobs that could be lost entirely, or skills. For example, in my portfolio, in terms of music, actors and so on, there are a number of concerns. We're also looking at what the advantages are, and we want that advantage. The Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy is in Boston this week, meeting business investors and the diaspora community. So, we are looking at the opportunities and the jobs that could come from AI as well, so that it's not just extractive, as we are seeing. Certainly, I will raise the fact that two Members—perhaps more by the end of this session—have raised AI with me, in order to ensure that we do update you and also engage with Members as this work goes ahead.
contributions.text_original: Yn sicr. Mi fyddwch chi wedi clywed y Gweinidog Cabinet yn sôn ynglŷn â'r manteision, ond hefyd y peryglon, ac yn sicr mae yna gydnabyddiaeth, o ran nifer o sectorau, o ran y pryderon hynny ynglŷn â swyddi a allai gael eu colli'n llwyr, neu sgiliau. Er enghraifft, yn fy mhortffolio i, o ran cerddoriaeth, actorion ac ati, mae yna nifer fawr o bryderon. Rydym ni hefyd yn gweld beth ydy'r manteision, ac rydym ni eisiau cael y budd hwnnw. Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni yn Boston yr wythnos hon yn cwrdd â buddsoddwyr busnesau a'r gymuned diaspora. Felly, rydym ni yn edrych ar y cyfleoedd a'r swyddi sydd i ddod gydag AI hefyd, fel dyw o ddim jest yn extractive, fel rydym ni'n ei weld efo pethau. Yn sicr, mi fyddaf i'n codi bod yna ddau Aelod—efallai y bydd yna fwy erbyn diwedd y sesiwn hon—wedi codi AI gyda mi, er mwyn sicrhau ein bod ni'n eich diweddaru chi a hefyd yn ymgysylltu efo Aelodau wrth i'r gwaith hwn fynd rhagddo.

contributions.text_english: I think it is very important that the Member should reflect on which Government you're referring to. You're talking about the Labour Government in your contribution there, whereas we are a new Government, in post since May. So, many of the questions were raised through scrutiny—and I was a member of the committee that undertook that scrutiny work—of the previous Government. Work is ongoing, and is being led by the First Minister, in terms of a new international strategy, which is looking at all of the offices, and looking at how we as a Government engage internationally too. He's been very clear that he wants us to be a Government that engages on the international stage because of the benefits to Wales of doing so. As the work on the strategy is updated, of course, there will be opportunities for Members to be questioning the First Minister and to be engaging and scrutinising.
contributions.text_original: Dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n bwysig iawn bod yr Aelod yn adlewyrchu ar ba Lywodraeth rydych chi'n cyfeirio ati. Rydych chi'n sôn am y Llywodraeth Lafur yn eich cyfraniad chi yn y fan yna, lle rydym ni'n Llywodraeth newydd ers mis Mai. Felly, mae nifer o'r cwestiynau a godwyd gan graffu—ac mi oeddwn i'n rhan o'r pwyllgor a oedd yn gwneud y gwaith craffu hwnnw—i'r Llywodraeth flaenorol. Mae'r gwaith yn mynd rhagddo, dan arweiniad y Prif Weinidog, o ran strategaeth ryngwladol newydd, sydd yn edrych ar yr holl swyddfeydd, o ran edrych ar sut rydym ni fel Llywodraeth yn ymgysylltu yn rhyngwladol hefyd. Mae o wedi bod yn glir iawn ei fod o eisiau i ni fod yn Llywodraeth sy'n ymgysylltu'n rhyngwladol oherwydd y buddion a ddaw i Gymru o hynny. Wrth i'r gwaith ar y strategaeth gael ei ddiweddaru, wrth gwrs, mi fydd yna gyfle i Aelodau fod yn holi'r Prif Weinidog ac i ymgysylltu a chraffu.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you. The Deputy Minister for Transport is here in the Chamber. What I would ask you to do in terms of the A55 is to write to him, and I'm sure that there will be an update for you on that.

In terms of the second statement that you request, I will raise this with the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care. Since you have met specifically with members of the workforce, then I think it would be a good idea for you to write to him as well, because it is important that they get that response. I understand, from what you say, that you have written, so I will ask him to ensure that he writes back to you.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth yma yn y Siambr. Yr hyn byddwn i'n gofyn i chi ei wneud o ran yr A55 ydy ysgrifennu ato fo, a dwi'n siŵr bydd diweddariad i chi o ran hynny.

O ran yr ail ddatganiad rydych chi'n gofyn amdano fo, mi wnaf i godi hyn efo'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal. Gan eich bod chi wedi cwrdd yn benodol gydag aelodau'r gweithlu, dwi yn meddwl byddai fo'n syniad pe byddech chi'n gallu ysgrifennu ato fo hefyd, oherwydd mae'n bwysig eu bod nhw'n cael yr ymateb hwnnw. Dwi'n deall, o'r hyn rydych chi'n ei ddweud, eich bod chi wedi ysgrifennu, felly mi fyddaf i yn gofyn iddo fo sicrhau ei fod o yn ysgrifennu nôl atoch chi.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I appreciate that this will cause temporary disruption in terms of the service for travellers while the railway is closed. The Deputy Minister for Transport has already published a written statement. If there are any additional concerns, then I would encourage you to write to the Member. He is here, of course, and he will have heard what you've raised. But, just to reassure you, the Welsh Government is engaging with Network Rail and Avanti and Transport for Wales through network north Wales meetings, and Transport for Wales and Avanti are completing detailed plans for bus replacement services during that closure period as well.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi y bydd hyn yn creu aflonyddwch o ran y gwasanaeth dros dro i deithwyr tra bydd y rheilffordd ar gau. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth eisoes wedi cyhoeddi datganiad ysgrifenedig. Os oes yna unrhyw bryderon ychwanegol, mi fyddwn i'n eich annog chi i ysgrifennu at yr Aelod. Mae o yma, wrth gwrs, ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi'i godi. Ond, i'ch sicrhau chi, mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ymgysylltu gyda Network Rail ac Avanti a Trafnidiaeth Cymru trwy gyfarfodydd rhwydwaith gogledd Cymru, ac mae Trafnidiaeth Cymru ac Avanti yn cwblhau cynlluniau manwl ar gyfer gwasanaethau bysiau yn lle trenau yn ystod y cyfnod cau hefyd.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for that question. In terms of a statement, it's not the norm to have a joint statement in that way. We do work across Government, of course, and certainly, if you were to write to the Ministers with specific questions, then you would receive that response. But, clearly, the Cabinet Minister for education leads on the pupil development grant, but there is close collaboration between Ministers where there is that overlap. What is important is that we do have that co-operation, because what we're trying to do is to always respond to Estyn recommendations. There is work, of course, for the relevant scrutiny committees in this Senedd and the cross-party group to be looking at such issues, to ensure that implementation is as it should be and that recommendations made by Estyn are progressed.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn hwnnw. O ran y datganiad, dydy o ddim yn arferol i gael datganiad ar y cyd yn y modd hwnnw. Mi ydyn ni'n gweithio'n drawslywodraethol ac, yn sicr, pe byddech chi'n ysgrifennu at y Gweinidogion efo'ch cwestiynau penodol, mi fyddech chi'n cael yr ymateb hwnnw. Ond, yn amlwg, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg sy'n arwain o ran y pupil development grant, ond mae cydweithio agos rhwng Gweinidogion lle mae gorgyffwrdd. Yr hyn sy'n bwysig ydy ein bod ni'n cael y cydweithio hwnnw ac mai'r hyn rydyn ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni ydy ymateb bob tro i argymhellion Estyn. Mae yna waith, wrth gwrs, i'r pwyllgorau craffu priodol yn y Senedd hon a grŵp trawsbleidiol i fod yn edrych ar faterion o'r fath, a sicrhau bod y gweithrediad fel y dylai fod a bod argymhellion sy'n cael eu gwneud gan Estyn yn mynd rhagddynt.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue, which received a lot of attention in the press last week, and I would like to say how brave those people who are speaking out about these things are, and it is terrible to hear about that suffering. The Deputy First Minister is here and will have heard what you've raised, and I would like to give you that assurance that we do acknowledge this, that the recent review of the national VAWDASV strategy has noted rural inequality as a key theme in terms of this work. Now, as the new national strategy is developed, I hope that the fact that we have identified this as something that is needed and deserves further attention—. As that review work continues, along with the feedback received, you will have an opportunity, as will others, to scrutinise the Deputy First Minister in relation to that work and to input as well.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater, yn amlwg, a gafodd gryn sylw yn y wasg yr wythnos diwethaf, a byddwn i'n hoffi dweud pa mor ddewr ydy pobl sydd yn siarad allan am hyn, ac mae'n erchyll clywed am y dioddefaint hwnnw. Mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog yma ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi, ond mi fyddwn ni'n hoffi rhoi'r sicrwydd hwnna i chi ein bod ni'n cydnabod hyn, bod yr adolygiad diweddar o'r strategaeth genedlaethol o ran VAWDASV wedi nodi anghydraddoldeb gwledig fel thema allweddol o ran y gwaith hwn. Rŵan, wrth i'r strategaeth genedlaethol newydd gael ei datblygu, dwi'n gobeithio bod y ffaith ein bod ni wedi adnabod hwn fel rhywbeth sydd ei angen ac sy'n haeddu sylw pellach—. Ac wrth gwrs, wrth i'r gwaith adolygu yna fynd rhagddo, gyda'r adborth rydyn ni wedi ei dderbyn, mi fydd yna gyfle i chi ac eraill graffu ar y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog o ran y gwaith hwnnw ac i fewnbynnu.

contributions.text_english: Well, tourism is hugely important for the Welsh economy, and the Member, I'm sure, will be aware that there are a number of challenges that have been faced by that sector, including the cost-of-living crisis. People have less money in their pockets. There is also the impact of Brexit, which has had an impact on the number of visitors to Wales and to our communities. You're referring to an area that is not implementing the tourism levy at the moment and referring to that as a barrier, and I don't really understand that. We have to look at the facts as they are. Every area will have its own challenges. We also know that there are opportunities that come with some of the things that are in train. But what we are committed to is ensuring that we work with Visit Wales to sell Wales to the world, that we want to ensure that tourism can prosper and that we support those businesses. It is central as regards what was in our manifesto and to the work that we are looking at on a cross-ministerial basis. As a Government, I, as Minister with responsibility for culture and sport, also believe that we're not taking full advantage of the tourism related to our history, our culture, and the opportunities that comes with major events such as the Tour de France and the Euros in 2028. Therefore, tourism is hugely important to this Government and we are working on a cross-ministerial basis on it.
contributions.text_original: Wel, mae twristiaeth yn bwysig ofnadwy o ran economi Cymru, ac mi fydd yr Aelod, dwi'n siŵr, yn gwybod bod yna nifer fawr o heriau sydd wedi wynebu'r sector hwnnw, gan gynnwys yr argyfwng costau byw. Mae gan bobl lai o arian yn eu pocedi. Mae Brexit hefyd, er enghraifft, wedi cael effaith ar nifer y bobl sy'n dod i Gymru a'n cymunedau ni. Rydych chi'n cyfeirio at ardal sydd ddim yn mynd rhagddo efo'r lefi twristiaeth ar y funud, gan nodi hwnna fel rhwystr, a dwi ddim yn deall hynny. Mae'n rhaid i ni edrych ar y ffeithiau. Mi fydd pob ardal efo'i heriau gwahanol. Rydyn ni hefyd yn gwybod bod yna gyfleon yn dod efo rhai o'r pethau sydd mewn grym. Ond yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo iddo fo ydy sicrhau ein bod ni'n gweithio gyda Chroeso Cymru i werthu Cymru i'r byd, ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau bod twristiaeth yn gallu ffynnu a'n bod ni'n cefnogi'r busnesau hynny. Mae o'n ganolog o ran yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ei roi yn ein maniffesto ni a'r gwaith rydyn ni'n edrych yn drawsweinidigol arno fo. Dwi, fel Gweinidog efo cyfrifoldeb dros ddiwylliant a chwaraeon, hefyd yn credu nad ydyn ni'n manteisio i'r eithaf o ran y dwristiaeth sy'n gysylltiedig efo'n hanes ni, efo'n diwylliant ni, a'r cyfleoedd sydd yn dod efo digwyddiadau mawr, fel y Tour de France, fel yr Ewros yn dod yn 2028. Felly, mae twristiaeth yn bwysig iawn i'r Llywodraeth hon ac rydyn ni'n gweithio'n drawsweinidogol ar hynny.

contributions.text_english: Thank you. The Member is quite right, this is a very important issue. I'm sure that all of us have had constituents getting in touch with concerns or who haven't been able to use public transport because they don't feel safe and don't feel that they can access services that are appropriate for them. Certainly, the Deputy Minister for Transport is present and has heard what you've raised, and he has expressed to me that he's willing to bring an update to Members through a written statement.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. Mae'r Aelod yn berffaith iawn, mae hwn yn fater pwysig dros ben. Dwi'n siŵr bod pob un ohonon ni wedi cael etholwyr yn cysylltu efo pryderon neu sy'n methu â defnyddio trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus ar y funud oherwydd nad ydyn nhw'n teimlo'n ddiogel ac nad ydyn nhw'n gallu cael y gwasanaethau sydd yn gweddu iddyn nhw. Yn sicr, mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth yma ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi, ac wedi mynegi i fi ei fod o'n fodlon dod â diweddariad i Aelodau drwy ddatganiad ysgrifenedig.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising those concerns. I don't know if you have written to the Cabinet Minister expressing those concerns—it's difficult for you to provide all of those details when you only have a minute to speak. But if there are concerns that we need to take into account, then of course we as a Government will do that. So, I would ask you to write to the Minister.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r pryderon hynny. Dwi ddim yn gwybod os ydych chi wedi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet gyda'r pryderon penodol—yn amlwg, mewn munud, mae'n anodd i chi roi'r holl wybodaeth hynny. Ond, yn sicr, os oes yna bryderon y mae angen i ni eu hystyried, wrth gwrs y gwnawn ni hynny fel Llywodraeth. Felly, byddwn ni yn gofyn i chi wneud hynny.

contributions.text_english:
I hope that the Member heard the oral statement last week. I don't think there has been a lack of opportunity to scrutinise and to ask the Minister questions. So, I don't think that a statement so soon after that is appropriate, in particular because, let's bear in mind, of what was noted, which was that we're now going to be looking at considering the evidence, understanding the different facts and options, and working towards solutions that improve journeys whilst supporting communities, businesses and the broader economy. So, as to all of the concerns that you have set out, that's exactly what will be happening now: listening.

I'm sure as well that the Member—like all Members here, I hope—wants to see this Government taking action. We have seen 27 years of a lack of action and a lack of solutions, so we have to move forward with this work. The engagement work is happening at the moment, and everyone with concerns has an opportunity to be part of this. It was announced last week that there would be more updates and opportunities for people to be engaging. So, I hope that we will be able to unite behind the fact that the Minister has outlined a way forward finally, and there will be an opportunity for those who have concerns to express those. But we do have to see a solution. I'm sure the Member agrees with me on that.
contributions.text_original:
Dwi'n gobeithio bod yr Aelod wedi clywed y datganiad llafar yr wythnos diwethaf. Dwi ddim yn meddwl bod yna ddiffyg cyfle wedi bod i graffu a holi'r Gweinidog. Felly, dwi ddim yn meddwl bod datganiad mor fuan wedi hynny yn briodol, yn arbennig oherwydd, beth am inni gofio, beth oedd yr hyn a nodwyd, sef ein bod ni rŵan yn mynd i fod yn edrych ar ystyried y dystiolaeth, deall y ffeithiau a'r gwahanol opsiynau, a gweithio tuag at ddatrysiadau sy'n gwella teithiau wrth gefnogi cymunedau, busnesau a'r economi ehangach. Felly, o ran yr holl bryderon rydych chi wedi'u nodi, dyna'n union beth fydd yn digwydd rŵan: gwrando.

Dwi'n siŵr hefyd fod yr Aelod—fel pob Aelod yma, gobeithio—eisiau gweld y Llywodraeth hon yn gweithredu. Rydyn ni wedi gweld 27 mlynedd o beidio â gweithredu a chael datrysiadau, felly mae'n rhaid inni symud ymlaen efo'r gwaith hwn. Mae'r gwaith ymgysylltu yn mynd rhagddo. Mae yna gyfle i bawb sydd efo pryderon i fod yn rhan o hyn. Mi gyhoeddwyd yr wythnos diwethaf y bydd yna ragor o ddiweddariadau ac mi fydd yna gyfle i bobl ymgysylltu. Felly, dwi'n gobeithio ein bod ni'n gallu uno yn y ffaith bod y Gweinidog wedi amlinellu ffordd ymlaen o'r diwedd, a bydd yna gyfle i'r rheini sydd efo pryderon i fynegi'r rheini. Ond mae'n rhaid inni weld datrysiad. Dwi'n siŵr bod yr Aelod yn gytûn ar hynny.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising these issues. You will have heard the First Minister's response last week, who also recognised the concerns expressed to him by constituents, and I'm sure we will all have received similar comments. The First Minister also outlined the review of the contract, which is exactly the issue the Member raised. You will be aware that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has questions next week. So, there will be an opportunity to question him further on this issue then, and I will make him aware that you have raised the issue today.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r materion hyn. Byddwch chi wedi clywed ymateb y Prif Weinidog yr wythnos diwethaf, oedd hefyd yn cydnabod pryderon roedd o wedi'u derbyn gan etholwyr—rhai y byddwn ni i gyd wedi'u derbyn. Mi wnaeth y Prif Weinidog hefyd amlinellu'r adolygiad o'r contract hwnnw, sef yr union hyn mae'r Aelod wedi'i godi. Mi fyddwch chi'n ymwybodol bod gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal gwestiynau yr wythnos nesaf. Bydd yna gyfle i'w holi fo ymhellach am hyn, ac yn sicr mi wnaf i o'n ymwybodol eich bod wedi codi'r mater hwn yr wythnos yma.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much to the Member for that question, and her wonderful Welsh, if I may say so. In terms of the issue that you raised, clearly this is a concern. And the issue of scabies was raised with me last week too. We will all have seen in the press and media those concerns expressed. I gave an assurance last week in terms of the steps that we are taking and our expectations of health boards in terms of disease control. Certainly, I will also ensure that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care is aware that a second request has been made for an update on that work. He will be answering questions next week, but I will see whether he thinks it's appropriate that there should be a further written statement on this issue.

Mi godwyd y mater o sgabies gyda ni yr wythnos diwethaf hefyd. Byddwn ni i gyd wedi gweld yn y wasg hefyd y pryderon hynny. Yn sicr, mi wnes i roi'r sicrwydd yr wythnos diwethaf o ran y camau a'r disgwyliadau sydd gennym ni o fyrddau iechyd, o ran rheoli haint. Mi fydd o'n ateb cwestiynau yr wythnos nesaf, ond mi wnaf i weld a ydy o'n meddwl ei fod o'n briodol i roi datganiad ysgrifenedig pellach ar hyn.

contributions.text_english: I formally move, Dirprwy Lywydd.
contributions.text_original: Cynnig yn ffurfiol, Ddirprwy Lywydd.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd, and let me also thank everyone who has taken part in the debate this afternoon. I want to be clear at the outset that I don't think that any difference of opinion has been expressed in this Chamber, and certainly I won't be expressing any difference of opinion in terms of what has been noted. I share the concerns that have been expressed. I have made that clear time and again. But if we look at the wording of the motion from Reform, that's where the disagreement lies:
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd, a diolch i bawb sydd wedi cymryd rhan yn y ddadl y prynhawn yma. Dwi eisiau bod yn glir ar y dechrau nad ydw i'n meddwl bod yna unrhyw wahaniaeth barn wedi'i fynegi yn y Siambr hon, ac yn sicr ni fyddaf yn mynegi unrhyw wahaniaeth barn o ran yr hyn sydd wedi'i nodi. Dwi'n rhannu'r pryderon sydd wedi'u mynegi. Dwi wedi gwneud hynny'n glir dro ar ôl tro. Ond os ydym ni'n edrych ar eiriad y cynnig gan Reform, dyna lle mae'r anghytundeb:

contributions.text_english: 'to ensure the Welsh Rugby Union protects the future of Wales’s four rugby regions.'

contributions.text_english:
It calls on the Welsh Government to do that. I can't give that assurance. That's what you're asking me to do: that I can give that assurance. And that's why I think that our amendment does reflect what we have heard today, which does create agreement between us all. We all want transparency. We're all insisting on transparency. We are also scrutinising, correctly, these decisions. But you'll also be aware that I'm here as a Minister and that many of the questions that have been raised today are questions for the WRU. Certainly, it is right that everyone from all parties does ask those questions, and I'd like to make it clear as well that I think it is important that the WRU listens to this debate today and responds to those concerns.

As we've already heard today, rugby is very important to communities throughout Wales. Many of you have mentioned that it is part of the identity of so many people—whether they're members of club, volunteers, players or supporters in every corner of our country. Many of you have also mentioned that it's part of our identity as a nation. The strength of feeling and the genuine concerns about this are clear, and I do recognise all of them. These changes are going to mean, if they come to fruition, that there would be a social, linguistic and economic impact. And that's why, as a Minister, I have challenged the WRU to show that the decisions are transparent, that they are evidence based and sustainable, and that the impact of any changes on players, fans, staff, communities and the wider game have been fully considered, as many have suggested, before any decision is made—not afterwards, but before. But we can't, as a Government, direct the WRU to maintain a specific structure for the professional game.

Mae'n galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i wneud hynny. Fedraf i ddim rhoi'r sicrhad hwnnw. Dyna rydych chi'n gofyn imi ei wneud: fy mod i'n rhoi'r sicrhad hwnnw. A dyna pam dwi'n credu bod ein gwelliant ni'n adlewyrchu'r hyn rydyn ni wedi'i glywed heddiw, sydd yn creu cytundeb rhyngom ni i gyd. Rydyn ni i gyd eisiau tryloywder. Rydyn ni i gyd yn mynnu tryloywder. Rydyn ni hefyd, yn iawn, yn craffu ar y penderfyniadau hyn, ond byddwch chi'n ymwybodol hefyd mai fi sydd yma fel Gweinidog a bod nifer o'r cwestiynau sydd wedi codi heddiw yn gwestiynau i Undeb Rygbi Cymru. Yn sicr, mae hi'n iawn bod pawb o bob plaid yn gofyn y cwestiynau hyn, ac mi hoffwn i ei gwneud hi'n glir hefyd fy mod i'n meddwl ei bod hi'n bwysig bod Undeb Rygbi Cymru yn gwrando ar y ddadl hon heddiw ac yn ymateb i'r pryderon hynny.

Fel rydyn ni eisoes wedi clywed, mae rygbi yn bwysig iawn i gymunedau ledled Cymru. Mae amryw ohonoch chi wedi sôn ei fod o'n rhan o hunaniaeth cynifer o bobl—eu bod nhw'n rhan o glwb, yn gwirfoddoli, yn chwarae neu'n cefnogi ym mhob cornel o'n gwlad ni. Mae nifer ohonoch chi wedi sôn yn iawn hefyd ei fod o'n rhan o'n hunaniaeth ni fel cenedl. Mae cryfder y teimladau a'r pryderon gwirioneddol am hyn yn glir, a dwi'n eu cydnabod nhw oll. Mae'r newidiadau hyn yn mynd i olygu, os byddan nhw yn dod i rym, fod yna effaith yn gymdeithasol, yn ieithyddol ac yn economaidd. A dyna pam yr ydw i fel Gweinidog wedi herio Undeb Rygbi Cymru i ddangos bod eu penderfyniadau yn dryloyw, eu bod nhw yn seiliedig ar dystiolaeth ac yn gynaliadwy, a bod effaith unrhyw newidiadau ar chwaraewyr, cefnogwyr, staff, cymunedau a'r gêm ehangach wedi'u hystyried yn llawn, a hynny, fel mae nifer wedi gofyn yma, cyn i unrhyw benderfyniad pellach gael ei wneud—nid wedi, ond cyn. Ond fedrwn ni fel Llywodraeth ddim cyfarwyddo Undeb Rygbi Cymru i gadw strwythur penodol ar gyfer y gêm broffesiynol.

I've heard many of you saying that you don't want me to be responsible for picking the team, and I'm glad that I don't have that responsibility. I'm not an expert, nor do I have the power to direct. The WRU is an independent governing body accountable through its own constitutional arrangements, and the WRU is responsible for the administration of rugby in Wales. Its independence is also recognised within the international framework established by World Rugby. That independence is important and it's important to recognise it. Issuing political directives on sporting decisions would raise serious legal and governance questions, and would threaten to undermine the independence on which international support depends.

The commitment sought by this motion is, therefore, one that the Welsh Government cannot provide. That's why, turning to the amendment, I've expressed a view that any significant change like this should be supported by a clear, long-term case, rather than a short-term response to the current challenges. We expect the WRU to explain how any change would support the future of the game in Wales and how progress would be measured.

The union must engage meaningfully with those whom the proposed plans will affect by conducting a full consultation and by explaining the evidence underpinning their plans, and they must be clear about how risks will be managed. Supporters and communities deserve more than warm words alone. You're right—many of you have mentioned that there is a need for transparency about the options under consideration and that we need to know the basis for any decisions, and how the long-term future of the professional and community game will be safeguarded.

As I've mentioned and shared in a previous session of questions, I met with the union in August and used that opportunity to convey directly to them some of the concerns raised with me through correspondence. In addition to that, following discussions in the culture and sport committee, and in the questions raised in this Chamber last month, and the range of correspondence that has reached me from Senedd Members on behalf of their constituents, I wrote to the union seeking more information about their engagement with supporters and communities, about the evidence guiding their approach, and how the union will assess and communicate the implications of decisions that are affecting the regional game. I'm still expecting a response to that letter, and, of course, I will update the Senedd once I've received any further information.

We need to be clear, therefore, that it's not the Welsh Government's role to run Welsh rugby from day to day, but I also want to give the assurance that this doesn't mean that we're not willing to scrutinise. We will continue to support participation, invest in facilities and work with partners to strengthen the game at every level. On the figure that was identified by some, in terms of £434,945 in 2025-26, which was provided by Sport Wales, this was, to be clear, to support the development of the game at grass-roots level. To put this in context, this represents 0.4 per cent of the total turnover of the WRU. So, that was for the development of the game at grass-roots level.

There's also been mention made of investment during COVID, and that was about a grant through the spectator sports survival fund. Reference was also made to the commercial loan of £18 million, which was fully repaid in 2025. So, the Welsh Government and Sport Wales do not provide funding for the professional game.

Today, as Members, you have expressed across the Chamber your concerns and you've offered a variety of solutions, but the one thing that is very clear between us all is that we have common ground, that we want to see a prosperous future for the game here in Wales and that we do recognise the genuine concerns that exist. That requires leadership, trust and a clear vision by the union. They have to treat supporters as partners in that conversation, not just informing them after a decision is made.

The loyalty of supporters has sustained the game through good and bad periods, and those voices should be central to shaping the future. So, while we sympathise with the spirit of the motion, we can't support a motion that asks the Welsh Government to guarantee an outcome that it doesn't have legal authority to enforce. But rejecting that motion is not the same thing as not recognising the concerns behind it; those concerns are real and they deserve to be heard, and it's vital for the union to respond to them. For those reasons, I ask Members to reject the motion but to support the Welsh Government amendments, so that we are united in our calls on the Welsh Rugby Union to consult transparently and to consider the voices of communities, clubs and supporters in shaping the future of the game in Wales.

Dwi wedi clywed nifer ohonoch chi'n dweud nad ydych chi eisiau i mi fod yn gyfrifol am bigo'r tîm, a dwi'n falch nad yw'r cyfrifoldeb hwnnw gen i. Yn sicr, dwi ddim yn arbenigwraig. Ond does gen i ddim ychwaith y grym i gyfarwyddo. Mae Undeb Rygbi Cymru yn gorff llywodraethu annibynnol sy'n atebol drwy ei drefniadau cyfansoddiadol ei hun, ac Undeb Rygbi Cymru sy'n gyfrifol am weinyddu rygbi yng Nghymru. Mae ei annibyniaeth hefyd yn cael ei gydnabod o fewn y fframwaith rhyngwladol a sefydlwyd gan World Rugby. Mae'r annibyniaeth hon yn bwysig, ac mae'n bwysig i'w chydnabod. Byddai cyfarwyddyd gwleidyddol dros benderfyniadau yn ymwneud â chwaraeon yn codi cwestiynau cyfreithiol a llywodraethiant difrifol, ac yn bygwth tanseilio'r annibyniaeth y mae chwaraeon rhyngwladol yn dibynnu arni. 

Mae'r ymrwymiad a geisir gan y cynnig hwn, felly, yn un na all Llywodraeth Cymru ei sicrhau. Dyna pam, felly, o ran y gwelliant, rydw i wedi cyfleu'r farn y dylai unrhyw newid sylweddol fel hyn gael ei gefnogi gan achos clir, hirdymor, yn hytrach nag ymateb tymor byr i'r heriau presennol. Rydym yn disgwyl i Undeb Rygbi Cymru egluro sut y byddai unrhyw newid yn cefnogi dyfodol y gêm yng Nghymru, a sut y byddai cynnydd yn cael ei fesur hefyd.

Mae'n rhaid i'r undeb ymgysylltu'n ystyrlon â'r rhai y mae eu cynlluniau arfaethedig yn effeithio arnyn nhw, gan ymgynghori'n llawn ac esbonio'r dystiolaeth y tu ôl i'w cynlluniau, a bod yn glir ynghylch sut y bydd y risgiau'n cael eu rheoli. Mae cefnogwyr a chymunedau yn haeddu mwy na sicrwydd drwy eiriau yn unig. Mi ydych yn iawn—mae nifer ohonoch chi wedi sôn bod angen tryloywder am yr opsiynau sydd dan ystyriaeth, ein bod ni angen gwybod y sail ar gyfer unrhyw benderfyniadau a sut y bydd dyfodol hirdymor y gêm broffesiynol a chymunedol yn cael ei ddiogelu.

Fel dwi wedi'i ddweud a'i rannu yn y sesiwn gwestiynau flaenorol, mi wnes i gyfarfod â'r undeb ym mis Awst, a defnyddio'r cyfle hwnnw i gyfleu'n uniongyrchol iddynt rai o'r pryderon a godwyd gyda mi drwy ohebiaeth. Yn ychwanegol at hynny, yn dilyn trafodaethau yn y pwyllgor diwylliant a chwaraeon, yr holl gwestiynau a godwyd yn y Siambr hon fis diwethaf, a'r ystod o ohebiaeth sydd wedi fy nghyrraedd gan Aelodau o'r Senedd ar ran eich etholwyr, mi wnes i ysgrifennu at yr undeb yn gofyn am ragor o wybodaeth am eu hymgysylltiad â chefnogwyr a chymunedau, am y dystiolaeth sy'n llywio eu dull gweithredu, a sut y bydd yr undeb yn asesu a chyfathrebu goblygiadau penderfyniadau sy'n effeithio ar y gêm ranbarthol. Dwi dal yn disgwyl ymateb i'r llythyr hwnnw, ac, wrth gwrs, mi fyddaf yn diweddaru'r Senedd unwaith rwyf wedi derbyn unrhyw wybodaeth bellach.

Mae angen i ni fod yn glir, felly, nad rôl Llywodraeth Cymru ydy rhedeg rygbi Cymru o ddydd i ddydd, ond dwi eisiau rhoi'r sicrwydd hwn: dydy hyn ddim yn golygu nad ydyn ni'n barod i godi llais, herio a chraffu. Mi fyddwn ni'n parhau i gefnogi cyfranogiad, buddsoddi mewn cyfleusterau a gweithio gyda phartneriaid i gryfhau'r gêm ar bob lefel. O ran y ffigur a nodwyd gan rai, o ran y £434,945 yn 2025-26 a ddarparwyd gan Chwaraeon Cymru, mi oedd hyn, i fod yn glir, i gefnogi datblygiad y gêm ar lawr gwlad. I ni roi hyn mewn cyd-destun, mae hyn yn cynrychioli 0.4 y cant o gyfanswm trosiant Undeb Rygbi Cymru, felly o ran datblygiad y gêm ar lawr gwlad oedd hwnnw.

Mae yna sôn hefyd wedi'i wneud ynglŷn â buddsoddiad a wnaed yn ystod COVID. Mi oedd hynny ynglŷn â grant drwy'r gronfa diogelu chwaraeon gwylwyr. Mi gyfeiriwyd hefyd at y benthyciad masnachol o £18 miliwn a gafodd ei ad-dalu'n llawn yn 2025. Felly, dydy Llywodraeth Cymru na Chwaraeon Cymru ddim yn darparu cyllid ar gyfer y gêm broffesiynol.

Heddiw, mi ydych chi, fel Aelodau, wedi mynegi ar draws y Siambr hon eich pryderon ac wedi cynnig datrysiadau amrywiol, ond yr un peth dwi'n meddwl sydd yn glir rhyngom ni oll ydy bod yna dir cyffredin a'n bod ni eisiau gweld dyfodol llewyrchus i'r gêm yma yng Nghymru, a'n bod ni'n cydnabod y pryderon gwirioneddol sydd yna. Mae hynny'n gofyn am arweinyddiaeth, ymddiriedaeth a gweledigaeth glir gan yr undeb. Mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw drin cefnogwyr fel partneriaid yn y sgwrs honno, nid dim ond eu hysbysu ar ôl i benderfyniadau gael eu gwneud. 

Mae teyrngarwch cefnogwyr wedi cynnal y gêm drwy'r amseroedd da a'r cyfnodau anodd, a dylai eu lleisiau nhw fod yn ganolog i helpu i lunio ei dyfodol. Felly, tra ein bod ni'n cydymdeimlo ag ysbryd y cynnig, ni allwn gefnogi cynnig sy'n gofyn i Lywodraeth Cymru warantu canlyniad nad oes ganddi awdurdod cyfreithlon i'w orfodi. Ond nid yw gwrthod y cynnig hwnnw yr un peth â pheidio â chydnabod y pryderon y tu ôl iddo; mae'r pryderon hynny'n real, maen nhw'n haeddu cael eu clywed ac mae'n hollbwysig i'r undeb eu hateb. Am y rhesymau hynny, gofynnaf i'r Aelodau wrthod y cynnig ond cefnogi gwelliannau Llywodraeth Cymru, fel ein bod yn uno yn ein galwadau ar Undeb Rygbi Cymru i ymgynghori'n drylwyr ac yn dryloyw, a gan gymryd lleisiau'r cefnogwyr, y clybiau a'r cymunedau i ystyriaeth wrth iddyn nhw lunio dyfodol y gêm yma yng Nghymru.

contributions.text_english: Can I ask on what legal basis you think I can force the WRU to do what you're asking? I think the amendment offers everything that you have just outlined. Isn't it time for us now to unite, on a cross-party basis, to ensure that we all get what we want? You have to acknowledge that I don't have the legal power that you have just said that you believe I have.
contributions.text_original: Gaf i ofyn ar ba sail gyfreithiol ydych chi'n meddwl fy mod i'n gallu gorfodi Undeb Rygbi Cymru i wneud yr hyn rydych chi'n ei ofyn? Dwi'n credu bod y gwelliant yn cynnig popeth rydych chi newydd ei amlinellu. Onid ydy o'n amser i ni uno, yn drawsbleidiol, i sicrhau ein bod ni'n cael yr hyn rydyn ni i gyd yn ei ddeisyfu? Mae'n rhaid ichi adnabod nad oes gen i'r grym cyfreithiol rydych chi newydd ddweud eich bod chi'n credu sydd gen i.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. There are no changes to this week's business. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to Members electronically.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Nid oes unrhyw newidiadau i fusnes yr wythnos hon. Mae busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael i holl Aelodau'n electronig.

contributions.text_english: There are questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care tomorrow, so it would be appropriate for you to raise them tomorrow during that session. If there's no opportunity to do that, I would suggest that you write with all of your questions to the Minister directly.
contributions.text_original: Mae yna gwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal yfory, felly fe fyddai'n briodol i chi fod yn codi'r rhain yn ystod y sesiwn honno. Os na fydd yna gyfle, mi fuaswn i'n awgrymu eich bod chi'n ysgrifennu gyda'ch holl gwestiynau at y Gweinidog yn uniongyrchol.

contributions.text_english: Thank you for raising those issues. You will have heard the First Minister stating unambiguously the commitment of this Government to look at and learn the necessary lessons from those experiences. You will also know the order of business in this Senedd. With the concerns that you expresses, I would suggest that writing to the First Minister would be best, because they were very specific issues that you raised. I think, in looking at the business programme, perhaps there wouldn't be space for such a statement for a number of weeks, whereas the issues that you have raised suggest that you need an answer sooner than that. Clearly, we are committed to continuing to update this Senedd and we will do so with all Members on this crucial issue.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i chi am godi'r materion hynny. Mi fyddwch chi wedi clywed y Prif Weinidog yn gyfan gwbl ddiamwys o ran ymroddiad y Llywodraeth hon i fod yn edrych a dysgu'r gwersi angenrheidiol o hynny. Mi fyddwch chi'n gwybod hefyd trefn busnes y Senedd hon. Gyda'r pryderon rydych chi'n eu codi, mi fuaswn yn awgrymu mai ysgrifennu at y Prif Weinidog fyddai orau, gan fod yna bethau penodol iawn rydych chi wedi'u codi. Rwy'n credu, o edrych ar y rhaglen fusnes, ei bod hi'n bosibl na fydd lle am nifer o wythnosau am ddatganiad o'r fath, ac mae'r hyn rydych chi wedi'i godi yn awgrymu bod angen ateb arnoch yn gynt na hynny. Yn amlwg, rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i barhau i ddiweddaru'r Senedd hon ac i ymwneud â phob Aelod ar y mater hollbwysig hwn.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising an important matter that I know is of great concern to Members in the wake of this news, and I know that the Government is in discussions with the company to understand what the implications are. I also understand that there is a topical question on this issue, which will be a matter for the Llywydd and Dirprwy Lywydd to consider. Certainly, we are very disappointed to hear this news. I know that this will create great concern locally and for those who face uncertainty in the broader community. So, I can provide that assurance to the Member that those discussions with the Government and the company are continuing and, certainly, I will ensure that the Cabinet Minister knows that you have raised this important issue today.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater rwy'n gwybod sy'n pryderu nifer fawr o Aelodau yn sgil y newyddion hwn, ac rwy'n gwybod bod y Llywodraeth mewn trafodaethau â'r cwmni i ddeall beth ydy goblygiadau hyn. Dwi'n deall hefyd fod yna gwestiwn amserol ar y pwnc hwn a fydd yn fater, wrth gwrs, i'r Llywydd a'r Dirprwy Lywydd ei ystyried. Yn sicr, rydyn ni'n siomedig dros ben o glywed y newyddion hwn. Dwi'n gwybod y bydd hyn yn creu pryder aruthrol yn lleol ac i'r rheini sydd yn wynebu ansicrwydd, ynghyd â'r gymuned ehangach. Felly, rwy'n rhoi'r sicrwydd hwnnw i'r Aelod fod y trafodaethau hynny â'r Llywodraeth yn parhau, ac yn sicr mi fyddaf yn sicrhau bod y Gweinidog Cabinet yn gwybod eich bod chi wedi codi'r mater pwysig hwn gyda mi heddiw.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I do hope that you took the opportunity to write to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care. There are questions to the Minister tomorrow here in the Senedd, and hopefully, you'll have an opportunity to raise these important issues. Let me be clear that patient safety continues to be a full priority for this Government. We expect every health board to have disease control processes in place in order to control cases effectively. I will also ensure that the Cabinet Minister is aware that you raised this issue with me today.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Dwi'n gobeithio eich bod chi hefyd wedi cymryd y cyfle i ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal. Mae yna gwestiynau i'r Gweinidog yfory yma yn y Senedd, a gobeithio y bydd yna gyfle i godi'r materion pwysig hyn. Yn sicr, gadewch i fi fod yn glir, mae diogelwch cleifion yn parhau i fod yn flaenoriaeth lwyr i'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydyn ni'n disgwyl i bob bwrdd iechyd gael trefniadau atal a rheoli heintiau cadarn ar waith i atal, adnabod a rheoli achosion yn effeithiol. Mi fyddaf i hefyd yn sicrhau bod y Gweinidog Cabinet yn ymwybodol eich bod chi wedi codi'r mater hwn efo fi heddiw.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much to the Member. I'm pleased that you agree with me that we do need a new culture and sport strategy, which will include a focus on the economy and tourism. I would encourage every Member to engage with that consultation, which is open until 18 December. I'm looking forward greatly to receiving Mike Hedges's comments as we develop that strategy.
contributions.text_original: Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod. Dwi'n falch eich bod chi'n cytuno efo fi bod angen strategaeth ddiwylliant a chwaraeon newydd i Gymru, a fydd yn cynnwys ffocws ar yr economi a thwristiaeth. Byddwn i'n annog pob Aelod i ymwneud â'r ymgynghoriad hwnnw, sydd ar agor tan 18 Rhagfyr. Dwi'n edrych ymlaen yn fawr at dderbyn sylwadau Mike Hedges ac i'w hystyried nhw'n fanwl wrth inni ddatblygu a llunio'r strategaeth honno.

contributions.text_english:
I hope that the Member will have heard the First Minister state unambiguously earlier that we totally condemn any antisemitism. I hope that we can be united as a Senedd on that.

Also, the Deputy First Minister, in her work as Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality, has been looking at the 'Anti-racist Wales Action Plan' to ensure that it is fit for purpose, reflecting on what we have seen in terms of the increase in hate of all types, including antisemitism. I will certainly raise your points with her.

In terms of your first point, clearly, digital infrastructure is crucially important; it's important for our economy. I know that this is something that the Cabinet Minister is taking seriously. I will raise the specific points that you made with him and ensure that there is an update on that work.
contributions.text_original:
Dwi'n gobeithio bod yr Aelod wedi clywed y Prif Weinidog yn gyfan gwbl ddiamwys yn gynharach o ran ein bod ni'n condemnio'n llwyr unrhyw wrthsemitiaeth. Dwi'n gobeithio ein bod ni'n unedig fel Senedd ar hynny. 

Hefyd, mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog, yn ei gwaith fel y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb, wedi bod yn edrych ar y 'Cynllun Gweithredu Cymru Wrth-hiliol' i sicrhau ei fod o'n addas i bwrpas, gan adlewyrchu'r hyn rydyn ni wedi'i weld o ran twf mewn casineb o bob math, gan gynnwys gwrthsemitiaeth. Mi fyddaf i'n sicr o godi efo hi'r pwyntiau rydych chi wedi'u codi efo fi heddiw.

O ran y pwynt cyntaf, yn amlwg, mae isadeiledd digidol yn allweddol bwysig; mae'n allweddol bwysig i'n heconomi. Dwi'n gwybod bod hwn yn rhywbeth mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn ei gymryd o ddifrif. Mi fyddaf i'n codi'r pwyntiau penodol y gwnaethoch chi ac yn sicrhau bod diweddariad o ran y gwaith hwnnw.

contributions.text_english: No, there will be no statement on this issue. As the Member has noted, this is an issue that is not devolved. But could I be clear, as I was in response to Darren Millar just now? This Government condemns all forms of racism, any idea that someone doesn't deserve to be able to live their life in the way that they have the right to live that life. Racism is a great problem in society now, and that's something that constituents tell us consistently. We all have a responsibility in this Chamber to ensure that we do support everyone that we represent, all members of society, and ensure that everyone feels safe, and that we all co-operate to ensure that racism doesn't continue here in Wales. There is no place for racism in Wales.
contributions.text_original: Na, fydd yna ddim datganiad ar y mater hwn. Fel mae'r Aelod wedi nodi, mae hwn yn fater sydd ddim wedi ei ddatganoli. Ond gaf i fod yn glir, fel oeddwn i yn fy ymateb i i Darren Millar rŵan? Mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn condemnio unrhyw fath o hiliaeth, unrhyw fath o roi'r syniad nad yw rhywun yn haeddu gallu byw eu bywydau yn unol â'r ffordd y maen nhw'n cael yr hawl i fyw eu bywydau. Mae hiliaeth yn rhywbeth sydd yn broblem fawr o fewn cymdeithas ar y funud. Mae hwn yn rhywbeth mae etholwyr yn ei ddweud wrthym ni yn gyson. Mae yna gyfrifoldeb ar bob un ohonon ni yn y Siambr hon i sicrhau ein bod ni yn cefnogi pawb rydyn ni'n eu cynrychioli, pob aelod o gymdeithas, a sicrhau bod pawb yn teimlo'n ddiogel, a'n bod ni i gyd yn cydweithio i sicrhau nad yw hiliaeth yn parhau yma yng Nghymru. Does dim lle i hiliaeth yng Nghymru.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising an issue that I'm sure a number of constituents have raised with us. I know that it's an issue that's been raised with me in casework. You will have heard me say that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has questions tomorrow, so there is an opportunity to raise this at that point. I would also ask the Member, if she hasn't already done so, to write to the Cabinet Minister to ensure that she gets a full response on this issue.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater dwi'n siŵr mae nifer o etholwyr wedi ei godi gyda ni. Dwi'n gwybod ei fod o'n fater yn sydd wedi ei godi gyda fi drwy waith achos. Fe fyddwch chi wedi fy nghlywed i'n dweud bod gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal gwestiynau yfory, felly mae yna gyfle i godi hyn bryd hynny. Byddwn i hefyd yn gofyn i'r Aelod, os nad ydy hi eisoes wedi, ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet i sicrhau ei bod hi'n cael ateb llawn ar y mater hwn.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising these issues. As you'll have heard me say, the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has questions tomorrow, but because of the concerns that you've raised and that there are specific examples, I would ask you to write to the Cabinet Minister and raise those specific concerns. Obviously, you haven't disclosed all the information here—it wouldn't be appropriate. But because of the nature of what you've raised, it's important that he does receive those details. You'll be aware that Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board continues to be at the highest level of scrutiny and that we are working very hard to ensure that oversight and scrutiny by the Welsh Government are present in order to target necessary improvements in patient care and the provision of services. And so, ensuring that the Cabinet Minister has that information is vital.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r materion hyn. Fel y byddwch chi wedi fy nghlywed i'n dweud, mae gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal gwestiynau yfory, ond hefyd, oherwydd natur y pryderon rydych chi wedi eu codi a bod yna enghreifftiau penodol, mi fyddwn i yn gofyn i chi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet a chodi'r pryderon pendant hyn. Yn amlwg, dydych chi ddim wedi datgelu'r holl wybodaeth fan hyn—ni fyddai'n briodol. Ond oherwydd natur yr hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi, mae'n hollbwysig ei fod o'n cael y manylion hyn. Fe fyddwch chi yn ymwybodol bod Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr yn parhau i fod ar y lefel uchaf o sgrwtini, a'n bod ni yn gweithio'n galed i sicrhau bod goruchwyliaeth a chraffu gan Lywodraeth Cymru yna er mwyn targedu gwelliannau angenrheidiol mewn gofal cleifion a darparu gwasanaethau. Felly, mae sicrhau bod gan y Gweinidog Cabinet yr wybodaeth honno yn allweddol bwysig.

contributions.text_english:
I thank the Member for raising this issue. Clearly, you will be aware of Plaid Cymru's commitment in terms of what you've outlined. The Deputy Minister with responsibility for this has heard the comments that you have made this afternoon.

Removing profit from the care sector is an issue that we worked on during the co-operation agreement, and that legislation is now in place and we're moving towards implementation during this Senedd term. The previous Government did sign a statement in 2025. As a new Government, we do support the principle of creating a care system that is more focused on families, is based on rights, is trauma informed, is locally rooted and is ambitious for all children, whilst removing profit from childcare and ensuring that no young person leaves care and goes into homelessness also. I do very much hope, given the fact that you will have heard this, Deputy Minister, that there will be an opportunity for you and the Member to discuss this issue further.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater yma. Yn amlwg, fe fyddwch chi yn gwybod am ymrwymiad Plaid Cymru o ran yr hyn dŷch chi wedi'i amlinellu. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog gyda chyfrifoldeb dros hyn wedi clywed yr hyn dŷch chi wedi ei godi heddiw.

Mae dileu elw o'r sector gofal yn fater y buom yn ei ddatblygu yn ystod y cytundeb cydweithio hefyd, ac mae'r ddeddfwriaeth honno bellach yn ei lle ac yn symud tuag at weithredu yn ystod y tymor seneddol hwn. Bu i'r Llywodraeth flaenorol lofnodi'r datganiad yn 2025. Fel Llywodraeth newydd, dŷn ni yn cefnogi'r egwyddor o greu system gofal sy'n canolbwyntio'n fwy ar deuluoedd, wedi'i seilio ar hawliau, sy'n trauma informed, wedi'i gwreiddio'n lleol ac sy'n uchelgeisiol ar gyfer yr holl blant, wrth ddod i ben â gwneud elw o ofal plant a sicrhau nad ydy unrhyw berson ifanc yn gadael gofal i ddigartrefedd hefyd. Dwi'n gobeithio'n fawr, achos y ffaith eich bod chi wedi clywed hyn, Ddirprwy Weinidog, y bydd yna gyfle i chithau a'r Aelod drafod hyn ymhellach.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising these issues. There is a clear commitment from this Government in terms of the fact that we are developing a national energy strategy that tackles these challenges and includes communities instead of doing things to communities, which is one of the points that the Member has raised. There will be an update to the Senedd as that work proceeds.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r materion hyn. Mae yna ymrwymiad clir gan y Llywodraeth hon o ran ein bod ni'n datblygu strategaeth ynni genedlaethol sydd yn mynd i'r afael â'r heriau hyn ac sy'n cynnwys cymunedau yn lle gwneud pethau i gymunedau, sef un o'r pwyntiau y mae'r Aelod yn eu codi. Mi fydd yna ddiweddariad i'r Senedd wrth i'r gwaith hwnnw fynd rhagddo.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I'm pleased that you do welcome this important investment. Certainly, this is something that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has committed to. We want to ensure that we do continue to ensure a health service that works for everyone, wherever they are in Wales. Certainly, I will raise with the Cabinet Minister the points that you've raised today.
contributions.text_original: Diolch am godi'r mater hwn. Rwy'n falch eich bod chi yn croesawu'r buddsoddiad pwysig hwnnw. Yn sicr, mae hwn yn rhywbeth y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal eisoes wedi ymrwymo iddo fo. Dŷn ni eisiau sicrhau ein bod ni yn parhau i sicrhau gwasanaeth iechyd sy'n gweithio i bawb, ble bynnag y maen nhw yng Nghymru. Yn sicr, mi fyddaf yn codi efo'r Gweinidog Cabinet y pwyntiau dŷch chi wedi'u codi heddiw.

contributions.text_english:
I thank the Member for raising issues that got quite a bit of attention, of course, when the First Minister made a statement on this issue some weeks ago, and made those very points in terms of nature-based solutions and the role of farmers too in this regard. And certainly, this is an issue that is at the heart of many of the cross-departmental discussions within this Government. 

To be clear, the First Minister leads on resilience, and then individual Ministers, such as the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, clearly have a role in terms of flooding and so on, and in terms of rural policy and farmers. So, that collaboration is important. 

There was a statement made. This was raised at that point as the work was proceeding. Of course, there will be further opportunities for Members to scrutinise, ask questions and have an input into that work.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch i’r Aelod am godi materion a gafodd gryn sylw, wrth gwrs, pan wnaeth y Prif Weinidog ddatganiad ar y pwnc hwn rai wythnosau yn ôl, a gwneud yr union bwyntiau hynny o ran datrysiadau o ran natur a rôl ffermwyr hefyd o ran hyn. Ac yn sicr, mae hon yn drafodaeth sydd wrth wraidd nifer o drafodaethau trawsweinidogol y Llywodraeth hon.

I ni fod yn glir, y Prif Weinidog sy’n arwain o ran gwydnwch, ac wedyn mae Gweinidogion unigol, megis y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd, yn amlwg yn cymryd rhan o ran llifogydd ac ati, ac o ran polisïau cefn gwlad a ffermwyr. Felly, mae’r cydweithio hwnnw yn bwysig.

Mi oedd yna ddatganiad. Mi godwyd hyn adeg hynny wrth i’r gwaith hwnnw fynd rhagddo. Wrth gwrs, bydd yna fwy o gyfleoedd i Aelodau gael craffu, holi cwestiynau a mewnbynnu i’r gwaith hwnnw.

contributions.item_title_en: Motions to elect Members to committees
contributions.text_english: I formally move the motions, Dirprwy Lywydd.
contributions.text_original: Dwi'n gwneud y cynigion yn ffurfiol, Ddirprwy Lywydd.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Llywydd. Two oral statements have been withdrawn from today's agenda, namely the national commission for Wales statement and the public and preventative health statement. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to all Members electronically.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Lywydd. Mae dau ddatganiad llafar wedi eu tynnu yn ôl o'r agenda heddiw, sef yr un ar gomisiwn cenedlaethol Cymru, a hefyd yr un ar iechyd y cyhoedd a iechyd ataliol. Mae busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi ei nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael i'r holl Aelodau yn electronig.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I don't know if you have written to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care on this particular issue. Clearly, the Minister will take questions later this afternoon in terms of our framework, but there's also of course an opportunity to raise such concerns. What the Minister has been unambiguous about is that we are holding health boards to account, that they need to be accountable for expenditure, and that is work that I know is at the heart of everything that he and his team of health Ministers are proceeding with.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Dwi ddim yn gwybod a ydych chi wedi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal ar y mater hwn. Yn amlwg, bydd y Gweinidog yn ateb cwestiynau yn hwyrach y prynhawn yma o ran ein fframwaith, ond mae yna gyfle hefyd wrth gwrs i fod yn codi pryderon o'r fath. Yr hyn y mae'r Gweinidog wedi bod yn ddiamwys amdano fo ydy ein bod ni yn dwyn byrddau iechyd i gyfrif, bod angen iddyn nhw fod yn atebol am wariant, ac mae hynny'n waith, dwi'n gwybod, sydd wrth galon popeth y mae o a'r tîm, o ran Gweinidogion iechyd, yn bwrw ymlaen ag ef.

contributions.text_english: Thank you. The Member will be aware of our commitment as a Government to be a Government for all of Wales, and that we do recognise the genuine challenges of this increase in prices—because of international affairs, mainly—and the pressure that's putting on residents, and it's a genuine pressure. Evidently, as the Member has mentioned, a number of these things are not within our responsibilities, but those discussions are happening. We as a Government are always looking in terms of the provision and the support that we can provide for those who genuinely are in difficulties because of these issues. Support is still available through the UK Government in terms of off-grid, and those are live and continuing discussions. But, certainly, I would agree with the Member; we do recognise that there are problems in terms of this that affect some communities specifically disproportionately, and they are live discussions.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. Mi fydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol o'n hymrwymiad ni fel Llywodraeth i fod yn Llywodraeth i Gymru gyfan, a'n bod ni'n cydnabod heriau gwirioneddol y cynnydd hwn mewn prisiau—oherwydd materion rhyngwladol yn bennaf—a'r pwysau y mae hynna'n ei roi ar drigolion, ac maen nhw'n bwysau gwirioneddol. Yn amlwg, fel mae'r Aelod wedi sôn, dydy nifer o'r pethau hyn ddim o fewn ein cyfrifoldeb ni, ond mae'r trafodaethau hynny'n digwydd. Mi ydyn ni fel Llywodraeth wastad yn edrych o ran y ddarpariaeth a'r cymorth rydyn ni'n gallu eu rhoi i'r rheini sydd wirioneddol mewn trafferth oherwydd mesurau fel hyn. Mae'r gefnogaeth ar gael, yn dal i fod, drwy Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig, o ran off-grid, ac mae'r rhain yn drafodaethau byw a pharhaus. Ond yn sicr, mi fyddwn i yn cytuno efo'r Aelod; rydyn ni'n cydnabod bod yna broblemau o ran hyn sy'n effeithio ar rai cymunedau'n benodol yn ddigymesur, ac maen nhw yn drafodaethau byw.

contributions.text_english: May I thank the Member for the work that she has done in supporting residents, and the fact that you have been unambiguous in your support for those residents? For the record, I would also say that I have raised concerns because of campaigning that I did as a local Member in relation to the impact that quarries can have on communities. I know that the discussions between you and the Minister are live discussions and that you are communicating regularly. I will certainly ask him to ensure that you are given that update, because it's important that we continue to make the case on behalf of the residents of Gwaelod-y-garth and other communities who will be concerned about this.
contributions.text_original: Gaf i ddiolch i'r Aelod am y gwaith y mae hi wedi'i wneud i gefnogi trigolion, a'r ffaith eich bod chi wedi bod yn ddiamwys o ran eich cefnogaeth iddyn nhw? O ran y record, mi ddylwn i ddatgan hefyd fy mod i wedi codi pryderon oherwydd ymgyrchu dwi wedi'i wneud fel Aelod lleol am yr effaith y gall chwareli ei chael ar gymunedau. Dwi'n gwybod bod y trafodaethau rhyngoch chi a'r Gweinidog yn rhai byw iawn ac eich bod chi'n cyfathrebu'n gyson. Yn sicr, mi fyddaf i'n gofyn iddo fo sicrhau eich bod chi'n cael y diweddariad hwnnw, oherwydd mae'n bwysig ein bod ni yn parhau i wneud yr achos ar ran trigolion Gwaelod-y-garth a chymunedau eraill a fydd yn pryderu ynghylch hyn.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this important issue. Evidently, you are not the first Member to raise this issue. We've heard questions to the First Minister specifically, and a commitment by the First Minister to learn lessons. Evidently, we were not in power when the decisions were made, but I do hope that that commitment from the First Minister was very clear to everyone that we want to ensure value for money, ensure value in terms of the site, and that that is a full consideration for this Government in terms of proceeding.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Yn amlwg, nid chi yw'r Aelod cyntaf i godi'r mater hwn. Rydyn ni wedi clywed cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog yn benodol, ac ymrwymiad gan y Prif Weinidog i ddysgu gwersi. Yn amlwg, nid ni oedd mewn grym pan wnaed y penderfyniadau hyn, ond rwy'n gobeithio bod yr ymrwymiad gan y Prif Weinidog wedi bod yn gyfan gwbl glir i bawb ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau gwerth am arian, sicrhau gwerth o ran y safle, a bod hwnna'n ystyriaeth lawn i'r Llywodraeth hon o ran bwrw ymlaen.

contributions.text_english: Diolch. First of all, on that second point, I'm so sorry that happened to you. I know it can be deeply distressing when such instances happen. I know that we are all at risk, and that is a risk acknowledged by the Welsh Government. Obviously, a lot of these matters are not devolved, but these are representations that we do make, because it impacts our democracy, it impacts the people that we represent, day in, day out, who are targeted in such a way. It's not just public figures. So, this is something we do take seriously. I would hope the UK Government does far more to protect citizens as well as those elected democratically. I saw recently comments from people saying that they would not be standing for council again because of such risks, so there is a risk to our democracy as well as a very real personal impact.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. First of all, on that second point, I'm so sorry that happened to you. I know it can be deeply distressing when such instances happen. I know that we are all at risk, and that is a risk acknowledged by the Welsh Government. I saw recently comments from people saying that they would not be standing for council again because of such risks, so there is a risk to our democracy as well as a very real personal impact.

contributions.text_english: On your first point, I'm sure that every Member here shares your concerns in relation to Admiral and Legal & General. The Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy will be meeting with Admiral this Thursday to discuss their plans and to understand the rationale better. This is a live situation, and certainly he will update the Senedd as we get a better understanding of the implications of this for Wales too. Officials and the Government will be working with both companies to see how we can safeguard jobs here in Wales.
contributions.text_original: Ar eich pwynt cyntaf, dwi'n siŵr bod pob Aelod yma yn rhannu'r pryderon rydych chi wedi'u mynegi o ran Admiral a Legal & General. Mi fydd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni yn cwrdd ag Admiral ddydd Iau yma i drafod eu cynlluniau ac i ddeall y rhesymeg yn well. Mae hon yn sefyllfa fyw iawn, ac yn sicr mi fydd o'n diweddaru'r Senedd wrth inni gael gwell dealltwriaeth o beth ydy goblygiadau hwn i Gymru hefyd. Mi fydd swyddogion a'r Llywodraeth yn gweithio gyda'r ddau gwmni er mwyn gweld sut rydyn ni'n gallu diogelu swyddi yma yng Nghymru.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much to the Member for raising this issue. I, and many Members here, I'm sure, have been involved in campaigns for the preservation of post offices in our own constituencies because of the crucial role that they play. Thinking of Bangor high street, of course, you do understand how important that service is. The Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality did meet with the Post Office today. Clearly, this is not a devolved service, but, because of the impact that it does have on people in our communities, these are ongoing discussions and, certainly, if any Member has similar concerns on Post Office services, as we do have regular meetings through officials, or through the Deputy First Minister, we're always willing to raise these issues.
contributions.text_original: Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Mi ydw i, a nifer o Aelodau yma, dwi'n siŵr, wedi bod yn rhan o ymgyrchoedd i frwydro dros barhad swyddfeydd post yn ein hetholaethau ni oherwydd y rôl hanfodol bwysig maen nhw'n ei chwarae. Wrth feddwl am stryd fawr Bangor, wrth gwrs rydych chi'n meddwl pa mor bwysig ydy hwnnw fel gwasanaeth. Mi wnaeth y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb gwrdd â Swyddfa'r Post heddiw. Yn amlwg, dydy hwn ddim yn wasanaeth sydd wedi ei ddatganoli, ond, oherwydd yr effaith mae o'n ei gael ar bobl yn ein cymunedau ni, mae'r rhain yn drafodaethau byw iawn ac, yn sicr, os oes gan unrhyw Aelod bryder fel hyn ynglŷn â gwasanaethau Swyddfa'r Post, gan ein bod ni'n cael cyfarfodydd rheolaidd drwy swyddogion, neu drwy'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog, rydym ni wastad yn barod i godi materion o bwys.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. Obviously, as the Minister with responsibility, I take it very seriously. That's why we're looking at the culture and sport strategy anew, which looks at how our historic sites are being treated, because there has been underinvestment and an underappreciation of the history of Wales, and that is something that we do recognise as a Government. There are formal processes that officials have to go through. I have said, of course, to Cadw officials to meet Members with any concerns, and, certainly, when I am in the area, I would be very willing to visit. It's also very important, and I would encourage any Member here—. The call for evidence for the new culture and sport strategy is open until 18 December. I want to hear from you about the things that are important to you and to those you represent. So, please engage in that process, because we need to tackle this issue.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Yn amlwg, fel y Gweinidog gyda chyfrifoldeb, dwi'n cymryd y mater hwn o ddifrif. Dyna pam rydym ni'n edrych ar strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd, sydd yn edrych ar sut mae ein safleoedd hanesyddol ni yn cael eu trin, oherwydd mae yna danfuddsoddi wedi bod a thanwerthfawrogiad o hanes Cymru, ac mae hwnna'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n ei gydnabod fel Llywodraeth. Mae yna brosesau ffurfiol mae swyddogion yn gorfod mynd trwyddyn nhw. Mi oeddwn i wedi dweud, wrth gwrs, wrth swyddogion Cadw i gwrdd gydag Aelodau sydd ag unrhyw bryder, ac, yn sicr, pan fyddaf i yn yr ardal, byddwn i'n barod iawn i ymweld. contributions.text_english:
I thank the Member for raising those two hugely important issues. Clearly, there was a great deal of publicity around Martha's rule recently, and, certainly, if we look at what we're trying to deliver across the health service in terms of Call for Concern, this tries to address similar issues. I know that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care would be more than happy to discuss this further with you directly. I'm sure that we are united in terms of those calls. It's a matter of taking action, and I know that there are different names for these practices in other nations—for example, it's Ryan's rule in Australia. So, it's important that we do operate according to best practice internationally in this regard.

In terms of the second point, the home-to-school transport issue, I think we would all recognise across this Chamber that this is a national challenge. I know that the Deputy Minister for Transport has been meeting with campaigners and has been acting in this area. The solutions are not easy. There are some things that are extremely challenging, but we do recognise that there are barriers at the moment that are creating difficulties in terms of school transport. I know that the Deputy Minister will continue to work on this. I would encourage any Member who has any direct concerns in terms of their own constituents to write to the Deputy Minister.

Dwi'n gwybod y byddai'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal yn hapus iawn i drafod hyn ymhellach efo chi'n uniongyrchol. Dwi'n siŵr ein bod ni yn unfrydig o ran y galwadau hynny. contributions.text_english:
I thank the Member for raising these issues. I do hope that you will have heard earlier today the response of the First Minister in terms of concerns raised about the financial settlement for local government, in terms of the important collaboration with this Government, and the recognition also that, as an opposition party, we did prioritise ensuring a better settlement for local authorities across Wales, and that that was a part of this year's budget that a number of Members of the Senedd voted against. So, if we want to safeguard public services, it is important that we do collaborate. That's the kind of attitude that we had as an opposition party, and as a Government, we're showing that commitment to collaborate with local government.

We also recognise, of course, the importance of the third sector. The third sector does undertake extremely important work, and in the wake of cuts that we've seen over a period of 15 years and more, they have become services that have had to take a great burden off other services that should be provided through the public purse. So, certainly, this is something that we commit to working on with the third sector on, and collaborating with local government, and I'd ask everybody here to consider how we can ensure that the funding is available, and fair funding for Wales as well from Westminster for us to be able to safeguard the third sector and local government.

I would ask you to review Joe Martin MS's comments on the cofnod and determine if you are of the view that he is guilty, in your view, of using disorderly, discriminatory or offensive language or language that detracts from the dignity of the Senedd. I thank the Member for raising that issue, and it was spoken about earlier today in First Minister's questions. I should declare that I share a constituency with you and I have been a strong advocate of taking action in terms of supporting communities who face this continuing risk. I've seen the impact that this has, not just when the floods happen, but any time it rains heavily, and that continuing fear that people have that they are going to suffer further flooding and the impact that that will have on their day-to-day lives.

The Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability will be making a statement in these next weeks about preparing for the winter. And certainly, what we have seen now, with this extreme weather, is that we have to do this work throughout the year, because one of the challenges that we have seen is that some of the storms happen earlier or later in the year, and that then that preparedness is needed. Certainly, that statement will be coming in the next few weeks. And I think, from what the First Minister said earlier today, that the work that we can do as each Member of the Senedd, in terms of supporting communities with that resilience and advocating for them, is incredibly important.

Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater a godwyd hefyd yn ystod cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog heddiw. Mi ddylwn i ddatgan fy mod i'n rhannu etholaeth â chi ac wedi bod yn eiriolwr cryf dros weithredu o ran cefnogi cymunedau sydd efo'r risg parhaus hwn. Rwyf wedi gweld yr effaith y mae hyn yn ei gael, nid yn unig pan fydd llifogydd yn digwydd, ond unrhyw dro pan fydd hi'n bwrw glaw yn drwm, a'r ofn parhaus sydd yna fod pobl yn mynd i ddioddef llifogydd a'r effaith y bydd hynny'n ei gael ar eu bywydau dydd i ddydd nhw.

Mi fydd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd yn gwneud datganiad yn yr wythnosau nesaf yma ynglŷn â pharatoi at y gaeaf. Ac yn sicr, yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ei weld rŵan, gyda'r tywydd mwyaf eithafol, yw bod yn rhaid inni fod yn gwneud y gwaith hwn drwy gydol y flwyddyn, oherwydd un o'r heriau rydyn ni wedi eu gweld ydy bod rhai o'r stormydd yn dod yn gynt neu'n hwyrach yn y flwyddyn, ac wedyn bod angen y parodrwydd hwnnw. Wedyn, yn sicr, mi fydd y datganiad hwnnw yn yr wythnosau nesaf. A dwi'n credu, o'r hyn ddywedodd y Prif Weinidog yn gynharach heddiw, fod y gwaith medrwn ni ei wneud fel pob Aelod o'r Senedd, i fod yn cefnogi cymunedau o ran y gwydnwch hwnnw ac i fod yn eirioli drostyn nhw, yn eithriadol o bwysig.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising that issue. The Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning will have heard your calls and the issues that you've raised. And I will discuss with her the most appropriate way of responding to those, be that a statement or by correspondence.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwnnw. Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio wedi clywed eich galwadau chi a'r hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi. Ac mi fyddaf i'n trafod efo hi y ffordd fwyaf priodol i fod yn rhoi'r ymateb hwnnw, boed yn ddatganiad neu drwy lythyr.

contributions.text_english: Thank you. The points made by the Member are on the record. I certainly know that Members representing other health boards have been raising concerns around parking in hospitals. So, it would be good to know about any problems so that we too can have those conversations with the health boards.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. Mae pwyntiau'r Aelod wedi'u nodi ar y cofnod. Dwi ddim yn siŵr os oedd yna gais am ddatganiad o ran yr ail un, ond yn sicr mi fyddaf i'n gwneud y Gweinidog Cabinet yn ymwybodol o'r hyn rydych chi wedi'i godi. Fel bob amser, os oes yna unrhyw enghraifft benodol rydych chi eisiau ei chodi, byddwn i yn eich annog chi fel Aelod i fod yn codi hyn. Yn sicr, dwi'n gwybod bod yna Aelodau sydd yn cynrychioli byrddau iechyd eraill wedi bod yn codi pryderon o ran parcio o fewn ysbytai. Felly, mi fyddai'n dda gwybod am unrhyw broblemau fel ein bod ni hefyd yn gallu cael y sgyrsiau hynny efo byrddau iechyd.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising that point. The Deputy Minister has heard what you've had to say. In terms of a more specific timetable, I don't have that information beyond what's already been shared with you, that is, that we do anticipate that the new guidance will be published in 2027. Officials are working with local government officers to update the guidance, and their feedback on the latest draft is being considered at the moment. So, that work is ongoing, and I thank you for raising the issue.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi hynna. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi'n ei ddweud. Mae'r swyddogion yn gweithio gyda swyddogion awdurdodau lleol i ddiweddaru'r canllawiau, ac mae eu hadborth ar y drafft diweddaraf yn cael ei ystyried ar hyn o bryd. Felly, mae'r gwaith hwnnw yn weithredol, a dwi'n diolch i chi am godi'r mater.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for the question. I would suggest that that type of question—. I didn't hear anything about a specific statement there. It was more of a scrutiny question, or a question for you to put to the Minister when you have that opportunity. But, certainly, the Cabinet Minister for Finance is present and she has heard what you've raised, and I'm sure you'll have an opportunity to discuss this further.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn. Byddwn i yn awgrymu bod y math yna o gwestiwn—. Doeddwn i ddim yn gweld dim ynglŷn â datganiad penodol yn fan yna. Roedd o'n fwy o gwestiwn craffu, neu'n gwestiwn i chi ei roi i'r Gweinidog pan fydd yna gyfle i godi hynny.
