contributions.text_english:
I thank the Member, and good luck to everyone who is involved in that welcome festival. And I look forward to attending Eisteddfod Bro'r Wenynen next year. As the Member has said, it will be an excellent opportunity for the area. And we know of the boost that comes to an area and its Welshness when Eisteddfod yr Urdd goes to that area. 

Certainly, one of the things that I felt very frustrated about as an opposition spokesperson was that there was not enough planning being done in terms of legacy. And the assurance I'd like to give the Member, and every other Member, is that I and the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language are having discussions at the moment about how to put that legacy framework in place in terms of the Urdd Eisteddfod and the National Eisteddfod, and you will have heard me speaking about other events across Wales. 

There is investment, of course, from this Government going into that, and ensuring that that legacy work does not just fall on the very busy people who are currently fundraising for these eisteddfods, but that we can work with people such as the mentrau iaith on the ground to ensure that legacy, is very important. So, as that work continues, I will be very ready to share that with Members, and to take your ideas and input on board as well. Because these are important events. They do leave a legacy. But if we can have more of a legacy by planning more strategically, then that's where I and the Cabinet Minister for Welsh education want to reach.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch i'r Aelod, a phob hwyl i bawb sy'n ymwneud efo'r ŵyl groeso sydd i ddod. A dwi'n edrych ymlaen at fod yn mynychu Eisteddfod Bro'r Wenynen y flwyddyn nesaf. Mi fydd o, fel mae'r Aelod wedi dweud, yn gyfle aruthrol i'r ardal. Ac rydyn ni'n gwybod yr hwb sy'n dod i ardal ac i Gymreictod pan fydd Eisteddfod yr Urdd yn dod yna. 

Yn sicr, mae o'n un o'r pethau roeddwn i'n teimlo'n rhwystredig iawn yn eu cylch, fel llefarydd yn yr wrthblaid, nad oedd digon o gynllunio yn cael ei wneud o ran gwaddol. A'r sicrwydd yr hoffwn i ei roi i'r Aelod, a phob Aelod arall, ydy fy mod innau a'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg yn cael trafodaethau ar y funud o ran sut mae rhoi'r fframwaith gwaddol yna yn ei le o ran Eisteddfod yr Urdd a'r Eisteddfod Genedlaethol, ac fe fyddwch wedi fy nghlywed yn sôn am ddigwyddiadau eraill ledled Cymru.

Mae yna fuddsoddiad, wrth gwrs, gan y Llywodraeth hon yn mynd i mewn i hynny, ac mae sicrhau bod y gwaith gwaddol hwnnw nid dim ond yn disgyn ar y bobl brysur iawn sydd yn codi arian tuag at yr eisteddfodau hyn, ond ein bod ni'n gallu gweithio efo rheini fel y mentrau iaith ar lawr gwlad i sicrhau gwaddol, yn eithriadol o bwysig. Felly, wrth i'r gwaith hwnnw fynd rhagddo, byddaf yn barod iawn i fod yn rhannu hwnnw gydag Aelodau, a chael eich mewnbwn a'ch syniadau chi hefyd. Oherwydd mae'r rhain yn ddigwyddiadau o bwys. Maen nhw yn gadael gwaddol. Ond os medrwn ni gael mwy o waddol drwy gynllunio yn fwy strategol, yna dyna lle dwi innau a'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg Gymraeg eisiau ei gyrraedd.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. Clearly, you are discussing an issue that is not devolved to this Senedd. If the Member wants contact details in order to raise any questions that he has in the most appropriate way, of course I would be happy to facilitate that. But, in terms of what is within the control of the Cabinet Minister, you are talking about an issue that is not devolved.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Yn amlwg, rydych chi yn sôn am fater sydd ddim wedi'i ddatganoli i'r Senedd hon. Os bydd yr Aelod angen y manylion cyswllt er mwyn codi unrhyw gwestiynau sydd ganddo yn y ffordd fwyaf priodol, wrth gwrs byddwn i'n hapus i ddarparu'r rheini. Ond, o ran yr hyn sydd o fewn rheolaeth y Gweinidog Cabinet, rydych chi yn sôn am fater sydd ddim yn ddatganoledig fan yna.

contributions.text_english: Thank you. Can I be very clear that antisemitism is something that we should all condemn? We should all work proactively to ensure that no-one is targeted in such a way and feels unsafe. The growth of antisemitism and hatred is something that should unite all of us in condemning and working hard within our communities to ensure that there is community cohesion and that nobody is targeted in such a way. The Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality leads on this work on behalf of the Welsh Government, though it's of course owned collectively by each of us, and the 'Anti-racist Wales Action Plan' is being reviewed to ensure that it's fit for purpose in light of the rise that we're seeing in antisemitism and hate crimes. Therefore, any Member here who is concerned about such issues, please engage with this work, because it's crucial that we work together.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you. So the Member will be aware, the Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality is the relevant Member; you asked at the start of your question who the relevant Minister was, so just to give you that assurance.

Could I make it clear? It has been unequivocal in terms of this Government that tackling poverty in all parts of Wales is a priority for us. Or entire programme for government, if you look at it, that cross-Government focus, in every portfolio, is entirely clear that tackling poverty is incredibly important and is something that we prioritise. The Member will also be aware, I'm sure, that there are problems in terms of rural poverty in particular that need to be tackled. Often, that has been something that has been hidden, and it's very important that the support that we provide in order to ensure that everyone, in all corners of Wales—. We know that, in every constituency, there are people living in poverty who should not be living in poverty, and that the last Labour Government's record was to increase the number of children living in poverty. That is why it is a priority for this Government to work across Ministers to get to the heart of the problem.

Diolch. I'r Aelod fod yn ymwybodol, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb yw'r Aelod perthnasol; roeddech chi'n gofyn ar ddechrau eich cwestiwn pa Weinidog a oedd yn gyfrifol am hynny, felly i roi'r sicrwydd hwnnw.

Gaf i ei gwneud hi'n glir? Mae hi wedi bod yn ddiamwys o ran y Llywodraeth hon bod taclo tlodi ym mhob rhan o Gymru yn flaenoriaeth. Mae ein holl raglen lywodraethu ni, os edrychwch chi, y ffocws traws-Lywodraeth hwnnw, ym mhob portffolio, yn gyfan gwbl glir bod taclo tlodi yn eithriadol o bwysig ac yn rhywbeth rydyn ni yn ei flaenoriaethu. Mi fydd yr Aelod hefyd yn ymwybodol, dwi'n siŵr, bod yna broblemau o ran tlodi gwledig yn benodol sydd angen eu taclo. Yn aml, mae hwn yn rhywbeth sydd wedi ei guddio, ac mae hi'n bwysig iawn bod y gefnogaeth rydyn ni'n ei rhoi er mwyn sicrhau bod pawb, ym mhob cornel o Gymru—. Rydyn ni'n gwybod, ym mhob un etholaeth, bod yna bobl yn byw mewn tlodi na ddylai fod yn byw mewn tlodi, ac mai record y Llywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf oedd cynyddu nifer y plant yn byw mewn tlodi. Dyna pam ei bod hi'n flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon weithio ar draws Gweinidogion i fynd at wraidd y broblem.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Work is under way to deliver a new culture and sport strategy for Wales. Through the new strategy, we will recognise the creative industries as central to Wales’s cultural life, economic growth and international profile. Creative Wales will continue to support talent, skills, business growth and opportunities across Wales’s creative sectors.
contributions.text_original: Mae gwaith ar y gweill i gyflwyno strategaeth ddiwylliant a chwaraeon newydd ar gyfer Cymru. Trwy'r strategaeth newydd, byddwn yn cydnabod bod y diwydiannau creadigol yn ganolog i fywyd diwylliannol, twf economaidd a phroffil rhyngwladol Cymru. Mi fydd Cymru Greadigol yn parhau i gefnogi talent, sgiliau, twf busnes a chyfleoedd ledled sectorau creadigol Cymru.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Well, certainly, you have a very creative constituency. I was very pleased to be in Wrexham last Saturday for the opening—well, the reopening—of Wrexham Museum, but the opening of the football museum there, that element of it. I am going to be visiting Wrexham again soon. I have been engaging in terms of the UK City of Culture. We are all crossing our fingers, of course, in that regard, and I will be very content to engage with the Member on that. Certainly, there are very exciting things happening in Wrexham. We want exciting things to continue to happen in Wrexham, and I'm very pleased to work with any Member who represents Wrexham in order to realise that potential further.
contributions.text_original: Wel, yn sicr, mae gennych chi etholaeth greadigol dros ben. Roeddwn i'n falch iawn o fod yn Wrecsam ddydd Sadwrn diwethaf ar gyfer agoriad—wel, ailagor—Amgueddfa Wrecsam, ond agoriad yr amgueddfa bêl-droed, yr elfen yna. Dwi'n mynd i fod yn ymweld efo Wrecsam eto'n fuan. Dwi wedi bod yn ymgysylltu o ran UK City of Culture. Rydyn ni i gyd yn croesi'n bysedd, wrth gwrs, o ran hynny, ac fe fyddwn i'n hapus iawn i ymgysylltu efo'r Aelod. Yn sicr, mae yna bethau cyffrous iawn yn digwydd yn Wrecsam. Rydyn ni eisiau i bethau cyffrous barhau i ddigwydd yn Wrecsam, a dwi'n falch iawn i weithio efo unrhyw Aelod sy'n cynrychioli Wrecsam er mwyn cyflawni'r potensial hwnnw'n bellach.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. May I be clear? There is creativity in every corner of Wales, but, because of a lack of support previously, a lack of a strategy and a lack of clarity in terms of support from Government, that potential hasn't always been realised. What the Member will have heard in my initial response is this Government's commitment to have a real culture strategy for Wales, one that includes the creative industries, that looks at skills, that looks at opportunities for people in Wales to remain here in Wales and to be creative here. That's the difference that you will see from a Plaid Cymru Government—that we appreciate the creative industries, that we want to work with them, that we want to see them develop and also want to secure more opportunities for people to work in an area that is of great economic importance to our nation.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Gaf i fod yn glir? Mae yna greadigrwydd ym mhob cornel o Gymru, ond, oherwydd diffyg cefnogaeth flaenorol, diffyg strategaeth a diffyg eglurder o ran cefnogaeth gan Lywodraeth, dydy'r potensial hwnnw ddim wastad wedi'i wireddu. Yr hyn y bydd yr Aelod wedi ei glywed yn fy ateb cychwynnol ydy ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth hon i gael strategaeth ddiwylliant iawn i Gymru, un sy'n cynnwys y diwydiannau creadigol, sy'n edrych ar sgiliau, sy'n edrych ar gyfleoedd i bobl yng Nghymru i aros yma yng Nghymru a bod yn greadigol. Dyna'r gwahaniaeth y gwelwch chi gan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru—ein bod ni'n gwerthfawrogi'r diwydiannau creadigol, ein bod ni eisiau gweithio efo nhw, ein bod ni eisiau eu datblygu nhw a hefyd sicrhau mwy o gyfleoedd i bobl weithio mewn maes sydd o bwys economaidd mawr i'n cenedl ni.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for those points. It's lovely to hear about all those excellent things that are happening in different constituencies. Creative Wales has supported bursaries for artists and production assistants from Wales to attend Rockfield Studios workshops, opening up access to expertise in the industry while supporting local activity and strengthening the creative ecosystem more broadly. I think the point that you make is that things like this don't happen by chance. You need a strategy, you need investment, you need collaboration. What we're seeing is that there have been major bands in the past but it doesn't mean that we're definitely going to have those bands in the future. It does concern me, and I have raised this concern previously, that there are fewer young people, for example, taking GCSE drama and music, that there are fewer opportunities and courses in terms of carrying on with music, but also opportunities to perform, which are just as important. We're very lucky in Wales that we have things like Battle of the Bands when it comes to the Urdd Eisteddfod and the National Eisteddfod and so on. These provide opportunities. But certainly, as part of the long-term strategy in terms of music, we have to nurture new talent and we have to create that infrastructure. As you mentioned, the announcement yesterday will help live music venues. We need to continue to work closely with things like the Music Venue Trust in order to ensure that there is an important future for them.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am y pwyntiau hynny. Mae'n hyfryd clywed am yr holl bethau gwych sy'n digwydd mewn gwahanol etholaethau. Mae Cymru Greadigol wedi cefnogi bwrsariaethau i artistiaid a chynorthwywyr cynhyrchu o Gymru i fynychu gweithdai yn Rockfield Studios, gan agor mynediad at arbenigedd y diwydiant wrth gefnogi gweithgarwch lleol a chryfhau'r ecosystem greadigol ehangach. Dwi'n credu mai'r pwynt rydych chi'n ei wneud ydy dydy pethau fel hyn ddim yn digwydd ar hap. Mae angen strategaeth, mae angen buddsoddi, mae angen cydweithio. Yr hyn rydyn ni'n ei weld ydy bod yna fandiau mawr wedi bod yn y gorffennol ond nid yw hynny'n golygu ein bod ni'n bendant yn mynd i fod â'r bandiau hynny yn y dyfodol. Mae e'n fy mhryderu i, a dwi wedi codi'r pryder yma o'r blaen, fod yna'n lai o bobl ifanc, er enghraifft, yn cymryd TGAU mewn cerddoriaeth a drama, fod yna lai o gyfleoedd a chyrsiau o ran mynd rhagddo efo cerddoriaeth, ond hefyd y cyfleoedd i berfformio, sydd yr un mor bwysig. Rydyn ni'n lwcus iawn yng Nghymru bod yna bethau fel Brwydr y Bandiau pan fo hi'n dod i Eisteddfod yr Urdd a'r Genedlaethol ac ati. Mae'r rhain yn rhoi cyfleoedd. Ond, yn sicr, fel rhan o strategaeth hirdymor o ran cerddoriaeth, mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn meithrin talent newydd a chreu y seilwaith yna. Fel rydych chi'n sôn, mae cyhoeddiad ddoe yn mynd i fod yn help o ran lleoliadau lle mae cerddoriaeth fyw yn digwydd. Mae'n rhaid i ni barhau i weithio'n agos gyda phethau fel y Music Venue Trust er mwyn sicrhau bod dyfodol pwysig iddyn nhw.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Sport Wales, on behalf of the Welsh Government, works closely with governing bodies, clubs and community sport providers to promote robust safeguarding policies, training and procedures. The Welsh Government expects all organisations delivering sport to take safeguarding seriously, to act promptly on concerns, and to ensure that children and young people can participate safely.
contributions.text_original: Mae Chwaraeon Cymru, ar ran Llywodraeth Cymru, yn gweithio'n agos gyda chyrff llywodraethu, clybiau a darparwyr chwaraeon cymunedol i hyrwyddo polisïau, hyfforddiant a gweithdrefnau diogelu cadarn. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn disgwyl i'r holl gyrff llywodraethu chwaraeon gymryd diogelu o ddifrif, gweithredu'n brydlon ar bryderon, a sicrhau bod plant a phobl ifanc yn gallu cymryd rhan yn ddiogel.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Welsh Government has been working together with other Governments across the United Kingdom. There was a 'Safe Sport Project Report' that was published in 2025. This was commissioned after intensive engagement with governing bodies, sport councils, athletes and people who have lived experience. Sport Wales represents Wales in terms of that work. In our first intergovernmental meeting as sport Ministers from all parts of the United Kingdom, we discussed this in Glasgow during the Commonwealth Games. This is an important issue. It is an issue that is not just relevant to Wales. Obviously, I will make sure that that work goes forward. Of course, if any Member is aware of any concerns, then we all have a responsibility to report on that and I would encourage anyone to make sure that that happens.
contributions.text_original: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi bod yn cydweithio efo Llywodraethau eraill ledled y Deyrnas Unedig. Roedd yna adroddiad prosiect ar chwaraeon diogel a gyhoeddwyd yn 2025. Comisiynwyd hwn ar ôl ymgynghoriad helaeth efo cyrff llywodraethu, cynghorau chwaraeon, athletwyr a phobl sydd â phrofiad byw. Chwaraeon Cymru sy'n cynrychioli Cymru o ran y gwaith hwn. Mi wnes i, yn fy nghyfarfod rhynglywodraethol cyntaf efo Gweinidogion chwaraeon eraill y Deyrnas Unedig, drafod hyn yn Glasgow yng Ngemau'r Gymanwlad. Mae hwn yn fater o bwys. Mae o'n fater sydd ddim dim ond yn berthnasol i Gymru. Yn amlwg, fe fyddaf yn sicrhau bod y gwaith hwnnw'n mynd rhagddo. Wrth gwrs, os oes yna unrhyw Aelod yn ymwybodol o le mae yna bryderon, mae'n ddyletswydd arnom i gyd fod yn adrodd ar hynny ac mi fyddwn i yn annog unrhyw un i sicrhau hynny.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Thank you for raising those important points. Central to the whole vision of this Government in relation to sport and culture is ensuring participation for all without barriers. That is part of our call for evidence at the moment, which will be open until the 18 December, so please encourage people to present evidence to that because we know that barriers exist. You've mentioned some of them, but there are others too. If we want everyone to have those opportunities, then, I agree with the Member, we must take action. So, I very much hope that, coming out of the new culture and sports strategy, ensuring participation for all will be a central part of the strategy, and I will be working with other Ministers, including the Minister for education and the Minister for social justice too.
contributions.text_original: Diolch am godi'r pwyntiau pwysig hynny. Yn ganolog i holl weledigaeth y Llywodraeth hon, o ran chwaraeon a diwylliant, mae sicrhau cyfranogiad i bawb a dim rhwystrau. Mae hwnna'n rhan o'n galwad ni am dystiolaeth ar y funud, sydd ar agor tan 19 Rhagfyr, felly plîs a wnaiff pawb annog pobl i gyflwyno tystiolaeth, oherwydd rydyn ni'n gwybod bod yna rhwystrau'n bodoli ar y funud. Rydych chi wedi crybwyll rhai ohonyn nhw, ond mae yna eraill. Os ydym ni eisiau i bawb gael y cyfleodd hynny, yna, dwi yn cytuno efo'r Aelod, mae'n rhaid gweithredu. Felly, dwi'n mawr obeithio, yn dod allan o'r strategaeth ddiwylliant a chwaraeon newydd yma, y bydd sicrhau cyfranogiad i bawb yn rhan ganolog o hynny, a chydweithio efo Gweinidogion eraill, gan gynnwys y Gweinidog addysg a'r Gweinidog dros gyfiawnder cymdeithasol hefyd.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
I don't know if my officials have had an opportunity to share with the committee yet the range of evidence that I referred to during my question session with the committee. I referred to the IWA report, the Institute of Welsh Affairs, which was independent and was not commissioned by Government. I referred to academic research that was also not commissioned by Government. There is a broad range of evidence out there. The work done in terms of the co-operation agreement emerged from that.

I would also encourage Members to look at the work done during the fifth Senedd by the committee that you're now a member of, which, on a cross-party basis, not from Government, was scrutiny work carried out by previous Members of this Senedd that confirmed that broadcasting isn't working for Wales as it currently stands, and encouraged Government to take action. So, what I'm doing as a Minister is acting on independent recommendations—listening and acting—and that's what I hope that any Minister would do in my position.
contributions.text_original:
Dwi ddim yn gwybod os ydy fy swyddogion i wedi cael cyfle i rannu gyda'r pwyllgor eto yr ystod o dystiolaeth roeddwn i'n cyfeirio ato fo yn ystod fy sesiwn ateb cwestiynau. Mi wnes i gyfeirio at adroddiad yr IWA, yr Institute of Welsh Affairs, a oedd yn annibynnol a ddim wedi'i gomisiynu gan Lywodraeth. Mi wnes i gyfeirio at ymchwil academaidd sydd hefyd ddim wedi'i gomisiynu gan Lywodraeth. Mae yna ystod o dystiolaeth eang yma. Mi oedd y gwaith a wnaed o ran y cytundeb cydweithio yn deillio o hynny.

Mi fyddwn i hefyd yn annog Aelodau i edrych ar waith a wnaed yn ystod y pumed Senedd gan y pwyllgor rydych chi rŵan yn aelod ohono fo a ddangosodd yn drawsbleidiol, ddim gan y Llywodraeth—. Roedd yn waith craffu gan Aelodau blaenorol o'r Senedd hon a oedd yn cadarnhau nad yw darlledu yn gweithio i Gymru fel ag y mae o ac yn annog bod angen i'r Llywodraeth weithredu. Felly, yr hyn dwi'n ei wneud fel Gweinidog ydy gweithredu ar argymhellion annibynnol—yn gweithredu a gwrando—a dyna dwi'n gobeithio buasai unrhyw Weinidog yn ei wneud yn fy sefyllfa i.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: I believe, and I would hope that every Member would agree, that we in Wales should have a voice and that decisions on Wales should be made in Wales. The fact that we don't have a voice as a Government in relation to what's happening in terms of the BBC charter at the moment, that we are consulted with just as any individual in Wales would be, and that we don't have a voice, really is unjust—that the future of S4C is reliant on decisions being taken in a Parliament that isn't here in Wales, without any need to take into account your views in terms of scrutiny, or my views as a Minister. It simply isn't working. That's why this Government is looking at the evidence in terms of establishing a shadow broadcasting and communications authority, to look at how it would work here in Wales. Doing that preparatory work to tackle problems—that's the intention of this.
contributions.text_original: Dwi'n credu, a byddwn i'n gobeithio bod pob Aelod yma yn credu, y dylem ni gael llais yma yng Nghymru ac y dylai penderfyniadau ynglŷn â Chymru gael eu gwneud yng Nghymru. Mae'r ffaith nad oes gennym ni lais fel Llywodraeth o ran yr hyn sy'n digwydd o ran siarter y BBC ar y funud, ein bod ni'n cael ein hymgynghori fel y mae unrhyw unigolyn yng Nghymru, ac nad oes gennym ni lais yn anghyfiawnder—bod dyfodol S4C yn ddibynnol ar benderfyniadau mewn Senedd sydd ddim yma yng Nghymru, heb unrhyw angen i gymryd ystyriaeth eich barn chi o ran craffu na fy marn innau fel Gweinidog. Dydy o ddim yn gweithio. Dyna pam mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn mynd ati i edrych ar y dystiolaeth o ran sefydlu awdurdod darlledu a chyfathrebu cysgodol, er mwyn edrych ar sut y byddai'n gweithio yma yng Nghymru. Gwneud y gwaith caib a rhaw i fynd i'r afael â phroblemau—dyna ydy bwriad hwn.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: As I responded to your previous question on this, there has been some financial support from Cadw for places of worship. We have been doing further work, and there is advice on its way to me. Once I've considered that advice, that information will be shared with all Members in terms of the next steps. But just to be clear, funding has been delivered to support places of worship—not the same kind of funding, but I will consider the advice that I will receive very soon. Thank you.
contributions.text_original: Fel y gwnes i eich ateb chi pan wnaethoch chi godi hwn y tro diwethaf, mae yna gefnogaeth wedi bod, yn ariannol, gan Cadw tuag at addoldai. Mi rydyn ni wedi bod yn gwneud y gwaith pellach. Mae yna gyngor ar ei ffordd i fi. Unwaith dwi wedi ystyried hwnnw, mi fydd y wybodaeth yna yn cael ei rannu gyda'r holl Aelodau o ran y camau nesaf. Ond i fod yn glir, mae yna gyllid wedi bod yn cael ei roi i gefnogi addoldai—ddim yr un math o gyllid, ond mi fyddaf yn ystyried y cyngor a ddaw ger fy mron i yn fuan iawn. Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Cadw does engage proactively with faith communities and the sector to understand better the state of our buildings of worship and the pressures that they face, including ageing fabrics, change in use, declining congregations, maintenance costs, and access to skills. Cadw continues to provide direct support through its own grant schemes. Over the past five years, more than £2 million of Cadw historic building grants have supported places of worship, which represents almost 20 per cent of grant funding. You will have also heard my response to the previous Member. I do expect further advice and guidance on this, and I will share an update once I've received that.
contributions.text_original: Mae Cadw yn ymgysylltu yn weithredol ag enwadau ffydd a chynrychiolwyr y sector i ddeall yn well cyflwr mannau addoli hanesyddol a'r pwysau ehangach y mae nhw'n eu hwynebu, gan gynnwys ffabrig sy'n heneiddio, defnydd sy'n newid, cynulleidfaoedd sy'n gostwng, costau cynnal a chadw, a mynediad at sgiliau arbenigol. Mae Cadw yn parhau i ddarparu cymorth uniongyrchol drwy ei raglenni grant ei hun. Dros y pum mlynedd diwethaf, mae yna fwy na £2 filiwn o gyllid grant adeiladau hanesyddol Cadw wedi cefnogi mannau addoli, sy'n cynrychioli tua 20 y cant o'r gyllideb grantiau. Mi fyddwch chi hefyd wedi clywed fy ymateb i i'r Aelod blaenorol. Dwi yn disgwyl cyngor pellach o ran hyn, ac mi fyddaf yn rhannu diweddariad unwaith dwi wedi derbyn hwnnw.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for those questions. The fact that we are consulting at the moment in terms of a new culture and sports strategy, and that we are looking strategically, is the perfect opportunity for every Member here to encourage constituents, to suggest to any societies, and Members themselves, to contribute ideas to that strategy. So, I would encourage you all to put forward these ideas, and we will then be able to look at the entire range of things that people in Wales would like to see us investing in. The one thing that I would say is that you are quite right to recognise the importance of so many of our places of worship, and the range of them that there is, and the story that they tell about Wales. So, thank you for raising those points.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiynau hynny. Mae'r ffaith ein bod ni yn ymgynghori ar y funud o ran strategaeth ddiwylliant a chwaraeon newydd, a'n bod ni yn edrych yn strategol, yn gyfle perffaith i bob Aelod yma i fod yn annog etholwyr, i fod yn annog unrhyw gymdeithasau, ac Aelodau eu hunain, i fod yn cyfrannu syniadau tuag at y strategaeth honno. Felly, byddwn ni yn eich annog chi i gyflwyno'r syniadau hyn, a byddwn ni wedyn yn gallu edrych ar yr holl ystod o bethau yr hoffai pobl yng Nghymru ein gweld ni'n buddsoddi ynddyn nhw. Un peth y byddwn i yn ei ddweud yw eich bod chi'n berffaith iawn i fod yn cydnabod pwysigrwydd cymaint o'n haddoldai ni, a'r amrywiaeth a'r stori mae nhw'n ei ddweud ynglŷn â Chymru. Felly, diolch i chi am godi'r pwyntiau hynny.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Thank you to the Member for raising those.
contributions.text_original: Thank you to the Member for raising those.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
I certainly agree with you. I was very proud of Team Wales, and not just those that won the medals; there were some wonderful and excellent performances, and we should be extremely proud of the whole team. As I mentioned in my appearance before the committee, when I was in Glasgow, to see that Wales had made such am impression, that they were everyone's second favourite team for everyone who wasn't from Wales, was wonderful to see. Clearly, there was some very sad news over the summer too, and I would like to take this opportunity to mention Fin Tarling. Our thoughts are with his friends and family. That was a disastrous occurrence over the summer.

In terms of our strategy now, I do want to ensure, in terms of major events—. I was very pleased yesterday that we saw that the UEFA Women's Champions League was to come to Wales in 2029. I'm pleased to say that that was one of my decisions as a Minister to support that, and that shows that we are taking action. But I have been very clear, too, that all major events that we bid for have to be for a purpose and that we will have considered, before making a bid, what the investment would be, but also what the value will be economically, socially, and outcomes in relation to that.

You and I have been here in the past and have seen Governments perhaps failing to outline what success looks like, and that is certainly something that I'm looking at now in relation to the Tour de France and also the 2028 Euros. But those measures and yardsticks should be in place before we bid, and we should have an idea of what we want to achieve. So, we are reviewing the major events strategy, and I will be taking that work forward. The work has commenced, but we will take it further.
contributions.text_original:
Dwi bendant yn cytuno efo chi. Mi oeddwn i'n falch iawn o dîm Cymru, ac nid dim ond y rhai a enillodd y medalau; mi oedd yna berfformiadau rhagorol yna, ac mi ddylem ni fod yn falch iawn o'r holl dîm. Fel roeddwn i'n sôn gerbron y pwyllgor, pan oeddwn i yn Glasgow, roedd gweld bod Cymru wedi creu cymaint o argraff, eu bod nhw'n ail hoff dîm pawb nad oeddent o Gymru, yn sicr wedi bod yn wych i'w weld. Yn amlwg, mi oedd yna newyddion trist iawn dros yr haf hefyd, ac mi fyddwn i'n hoffi cymryd y cyfle yma i sôn am Fin Tarling. Mae ein meddyliau ni i gyd efo'i deulu a'i ffrindiau. Roedd hynny'n drychinebus dros yr haf.

O ran ein strategaeth ni rŵan, dwi eisiau sicrhau, o ran digwyddiadau mawr—. Roeddwn i'n falch iawn ddoe ein bod ni wedi gweld bod Champions League y menywod yn dod i Gymru yn 2029. Dwi'n falch i ddweud mai un o fy mhenderfyniadau i fel Gweinidog oedd cefnogi hwnna, ac mae hwnna'n dangos ein bod ni'n gweithredu. Ond dwi wedi bod yn glir iawn hefyd fod yn rhaid i'r holl ddigwyddiadau mawr rydyn ni'n mynd amdanyn nhw fod i bwrpas a'n bod ni wedi ystyried, cyn ein bod ni'n ymgeisio, beth fydd y buddsoddiad, ond hefyd beth ydy'r gwerth yn economaidd, yn gymdeithasol a'r deilliannau o ran hynny.

Mi ydych chi a minnau wedi bod yma yn y gorffennol a gweld Llywodraethau efallai'n methu â dweud beth ydy'r mesurau, sut rydyn ni'n mesur llwyddiant, ac mae hwnna'n sicr yn rhywbeth dwi'n edrych arno rŵan fel Gweinidog o ran y Tour de France a hefyd Ewros 2028. Ond mi ddylai'r mesurau yna fod yn eu lle cyn inni fod yn ymgeisio, a syniad o beth rydyn ni eisiau cael allan ohonyn nhw. Felly, mi ydyn ni'n ailedrych ar y strategaeth digwyddiadau mawr hefyd, ac mi fydda i'n mynd â'r gwaith yma rhagddo. Mae gwaith wedi dechrau, ond rydyn ni'n mynd â hwnna ymhellach hefyd.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
I'm glad that the Member referenced the work that we've prioritised in terms of understanding the need, because the thing that I'm determined to do is have a plan in place long term, because, as I said in evidence to the committee, we do know, in some sectors, the investments needed, and the figures are eye-watering. They're not the kind of finances that we have currently available, they're nowhere near enough what's needed, and we will need to look strategically once we know that full picture.

I completely agree with you—and I think I mentioned this in my response to Mike Hedges during committee on Monday, when he asked me about bidding for the Commonwealth Games—we can't just invest in facilities to attract major events if then it means there's no money left to invest in key infrastructure like our swimming pools, like 3G pitches and so on, and that means that people in your constituency, in other constituencies across Wales, then fail to have access. So, this work will then be able to outline what investment is needed, where public investment is needed, how we work with local authorities, work with different budgets, because there are investments made in schools, for instance, in sport facilities.

The guarantee I give you is that we will have that long-term strategic approach, working with national governing bodies, Sport Wales, working with local authorities, working across portfolios, to ensure that we identify where the gaps are, where infrastructure is at point of failure as well, because we know a number of swimming pools are extremely old across Wales and are at risk of not being financially viable or able to stay open. We know some have closed already. That's my commitment. We want to see the right facilities that people will be able to use so they can stay active, be active in their communities, and that means every corner of Wales, rural Wales, including urban.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: I met WRU representatives in August and discussed their plans for the future of the professional game. I made clear the importance of open and meaningful engagement with regions, supporters and communities, and of ensuring that any decisions are transparent, evidence based and take full account of the wider impact on Welsh rugby.
contributions.text_original: Mi wnes i gwrdd â chynrychiolwyr o Undeb Rygbi Cymru ym mis Awst a thrafod eu cynlluniau ar gyfer dyfodol y gêm broffesiynol. Fe wnes i wneud yn glir bwysigrwydd ymgysylltu agored ac ystyrlon gyda rhanbarthau, cefnogwyr a chymunedau, a sicrhau bod unrhyw benderfyniadau yn dryloyw, yn seiliedig ar dystiolaeth ac yn ystyried yr effaith ehangach ar rygbi Cymru.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Can I thank the Member, in the first instance, for the communication that you've had with me on this topic, as well as your fellow Members for Gŵyr Abertawe, and also every Member who has contacted me on this important matter? Rugby is more than just a sport, isn't it? People feel it to the quick. It's part of the identity of communities, as you have mentioned here. And that transparency is important, because this is about more than just a location, it's more than just the economic impact; it's about that community spirit and feeling. So certainly, as I said in my initial answer, I said very clearly to the WRU that we do expect transparency, we expect that collaboration with communities, and that's my message again today.
contributions.text_original: A gaf i ddiolch i'r Aelod, yn gyntaf, am y cyfathrebu rydych chi wedi'i wneud efo fi dros y pwnc yma, ynghyd â'ch Aelodau chi dros Ŵyr Abertawe, a hefyd i bob Aelod sydd wedi ymgysylltu efo fi dros y mater pwysig hwn? Mae rygbi yn fwy na champ, onid ydy? Mae pobl yn ei deimlo fo i'r byw; mae o'n rhan o hunaniaeth cymunedau, fel rydych chi wedi sôn fan hyn. Mae'r tryloywder yna'n bwysig, oherwydd mae hyn am fwy na lleoliad, mae'n fwy nag effaith economaidd; mae ynglŷn â'r ymdeimlad cymunedol yna. Felly, yn sicr, fel y gwnes i ddweud yn fy ymateb cychwynnol, mi ddywedais i'n glir wrth Undeb Rygbi Cymru ein bod ni'n disgwyl y tryloywder yna, ein bod ni'n disgwyl y cydweithio efo cymunedau, a dyna fy neges i eto heddiw.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Thank you for raising those concerns. It is essential that this process is conducted in a way that is transparent, evidence-based, and accountable. Supporters, players, volunteers, local communities and elected Members must have confidence that decisions are being taken with a full understanding of the wider impact and that their views have been properly considered. In any subsequent conversations with the Welsh Rugby Union—I do meet with them regularly—I will, of course, express the views that have been expressed to me.
contributions.text_original: Thank you for raising those concerns. It is essential that this process is conducted in a way that is transparent, evidence-based, and accountable. Supporters, players, volunteers, local communities and elected Members must have confidence that decisions are being taken with a full understanding of the wider impact and that their views have been properly considered. In any subsequent conversations with the Welsh Rugby Union—I do meet with them regularly—I will, of course, express the views that have been expressed to me.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: As I've already outlined this afternoon, the WRU is the independent governing body for rugby in Wales and is responsible for decisions about the structure and development of the professional game, including in north Wales. The Welsh Government does not fund professional sports teams, but through Sport Wales we support the community and the grass-roots game.
contributions.text_original: Fel dwi wedi amlinellu eisoes heddiw, mae Undeb Rygbi Cymru yn gorff llywodraethu annibynnol ar gyfer rygbi yng Nghymru ac mae'n gyfrifol am benderfyniadau ynghylch strwythur a datblygiad y gêm broffesiynol, gan gynnwys yng ngogledd Cymru. Nid yw Llywodraeth Cymru yn ariannu timau chwaraeon proffesiynol, ond trwy Chwaraeon Cymru rydyn ni yn cefnogi'r gymuned a'r gêm ar lawr gwlad.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
As I said in my initial response, it's the WRU that is the independent governing body and they have responsibility in this area, but, of course, I do have opportunities in my meetings with them to express any concerns that have been raised with me.

In terms of rugby in north Wales, I do recognise the strong ambition and the increasing popularity of and participation in rugby in north Wales, and I support the development of the game at all levels. We want talented players from north Wales to have clear pathways to get to the elite levels of the game within their communities, without having to move from north Wales. I have read concerns that this isn't currently possible, so I thank the Member for raising the issue with me.
contributions.text_original:
Fel gwnes i ddweud yn fy ymateb cyntaf, Undeb Rygbi Cymru ydy'r corff llywodraethu annibynnol a nhw sydd efo'r cyfrifoldeb, ond mae gen i, wrth gwrs, gyfleoedd yn fy nghyfarfodydd gyda nhw i fynegi unrhyw bryderon sy'n cael eu codi gyda ni.

O ran rygbi gogledd Cymru, dwi yn cydnabod yr uchelgais gref a'r cyfranogiad rygbi cynyddol ledled gogledd Cymru, a dwi'n cefnogi datblygiad y gêm ar bob lefel. Mi ydyn ni eisiau i chwaraewyr talentog o ogledd Cymru gael llwybrau clir i gyrraedd lefelau uchaf y gêm o fewn eu cymunedau, heb orfod symud o ogledd Cymru. A dwi wedi darllen y pryderon nad ydy hynny'n bosib ar y funud, felly diolch i'r Aelod am godi hynna gyda fi.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Thank you. As I mentioned, this isn't the responsibility of Welsh Government, but, certainly, we would want to work with the WRU and different governing bodies in terms of equal access to sport. In terms of the points that you raise, I would suggest that you also raise them with the WRU directly. It is important that we do act in the interests of constituents in terms of local clubs, But, certainly, as I told Janet Finch-Saunders, we certainly want opportunities for young people to remain here in Wales and to play at the highest levels, and we recognise that that isn't currently happening.
contributions.text_original: Diolch. Fel oeddwn i'n dweud, nid cyfrifoldeb Llywodraeth Cymru mo hynny, ond yn sicr mi fyddwn ni eisiau cydweithio efo Undeb Rygbi Cymru a gwahanol gyrff llywodraethu eraill o ran mynediad cyfartal i chwaraeon. O ran y pwyntiau dŷch chi'n eu codi, mi fyddwn i'n argymell eich bod chi'n eu codi nhw hefyd efo Undeb Rygbi Cymru yn uniongyrchol. Mae'n bwysig ein bod ni yn gweithredu ar ran etholwyr o ran clybiau lleol. Ond yn sicr, fel dywedais i wrth Janet Finch-Saunders, dŷn ni eisiau cyfleoedd i bobl ifanc allu parhau yma yng Nghymru i chwarae ar y lefel uchaf, a dŷn ni'n cydnabod nad yw hynny yn digwydd ar y funud.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: The Welsh Government supports rugby participation in Clwyd through our investment in grass-roots sport, delivered through Sport Wales. This helps clubs improve facilities, reduce running costs and create more opportunities for people of all ages and backgrounds to take part.
contributions.text_original: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi cyfranogiad rygbi yng Nghlwyd drwy ein buddsoddiad mewn chwaraeon ar lawr gwlad, a ddarperir drwy Chwaraeon Cymru. Mae hyn yn helpu clybiau i wella cyfleusterau, lleihau costau rhedeg a chreu mwy o gyfleoedd i bobl o bob oed a chefndir gymryd rhan.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: It's not the Welsh Government that decides on that investment. It's a matter for the individual sports bodies but also for Sport Wales. What we have made as a commitment as a Government is that we want to ensure that there is investment across Wales and an opportunity for everyone to participate wherever they live in Wales. And the strategic review that we're carrying out in terms of where investment is needed works together with the WRU, FAW, Swim Wales and others to ensure that that is a plan that is supported by everyone, not just by the Government but by these bodies as well. Work will also be done to work with local authorities in terms of that too.
contributions.text_original: Nid Llywodraeth Cymru sy'n penderfynu ar y buddsoddiad hwnnw. Mae e'n fater i gyrff chwaraeon unigol ond hefyd i Chwaraeon Cymru. Yr hyn sydd gennym ni fel ymrwymiad fel Llywodraeth ydy ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau bod yna fuddsoddiad ledled Cymru, cyfle i bawb gyfranogi lle bynnag eu bod yn byw yng Nghymru. Ac mae'r adolygiad strategol dŷn ni'n ei wneud o ran lle mae angen buddsoddiad yn cydweithio gydag Undeb Rygbi Cymru, Cymdeithas Pêl-droed Cymru, Nofio Cymru ac eraill i sicrhau bod hwnnw'n gynllun sy'n cael ei gefnogi gan bawb, nid dim ond gan y Llywodraeth ond gan y cyrff hyn hefyd. Bydd yna waith hefyd i weithio efo awdurdodau lleol o ran hynny.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
Thank you for raising those important points. Working with the WRU, we want to ensure—. As I said, it's very important that everyone has the opportunity to participate, and when there are barriers to that, then that is a challenge that I am ready to put to the WRU or to put to any body where that isn't working as it should.

There is some data that shows that there is some good news in terms of women and girls in Wales. Some 90 per cent of players now move from the under-14 pathway to that for under-16s in terms of rugby, which is an important step forward. But, obviously, we then need to understand what else needs to be done, and this is something that's very live to us in terms of discussions between officials and the WRU and all of the sporting bodies in Wales.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch am godi'r pwyntiau pwysig yna. Wrth gydweithio gydag Undeb Rygbi Cymru dŷn ni eisiau sicrhau—. Fel roeddwn i'n dweud, mae'n bwysig iawn fod pawb yn cael y cyfle i gyfranogi, a phan mae yna rwystrau i hynny, yna mae hwnna'n her dwi'n barod iawn i'w rhoi i Undeb Rygbi Cymru neu ei rhoi i unrhyw gorff lle nad yw hynny'n gweithio.

Mae peth data yn dangos bod yna beth newydd da o ran merched yng Nghymru. Mae 90 y cant o chwaraewyr rŵan yn symud o'r pathway dan 14 i dan 16 o ran rygbi, sydd yn gam pwysig yn ei flaen. Ond, yn amlwg, mae angen deall wedyn beth arall sydd angen cael ei wneud, ac mae hwn yn rhywbeth byw iawn o ran trafodaethau rhwng swyddogion, Undeb Rygbi Cymru a holl gyrff chwaraeon yng Nghymru.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: The Welsh Government supports library facilities in Casnewydd Islwyn through capital and revenue funding for the development of libraries. This includes £200,000 in capital funding to transform the children's library in Newport Central Library. Libraries in Casnewydd Islwyn have also benefited from over £22,000 for small grant project programmes.
contributions.text_original: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n cefnogi cyfleusterau llyfrgell yng Nghasnewydd Islwyn drwy gyllid cyfalaf a refeniw ar gyfer datblygu llyfrgelloedd. Mae hyn yn cynnwys £200,000 o gyllid cyfalaf i drawsnewid y llyfrgell i blant yn Llyfrgell Ganolog Casnewydd. Mae llyfrgelloedd Casnewydd Islwyn hefyd wedi elwa o dros £22,000 ar gyfer cyllid prosiectau grantiau bach.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
You raise an extremely important point, and I don't have the powers to intervene in that manner, but what I am doing at the moment, through the work that we are doing, is to understand what the situation actually is in terms of libraries the length and breadth of Wales. They're a statutory service. We know that there have been cuts across Wales. Many Members here will have campaigned to retain their local libraries, and I am deeply concerned about the future of our libraries—the future in terms of that investment.

We need to understand what the situation is, and that is why, in terms of a long-term vision and strategy and to be clear on the long-term investment needed, I can give an assurance to the Member that I do believe that libraries are important, that this work is ongoing, and that we would want to work with local authorities, certainly, in order to ensure that the right services exist in our communities and that there is access to our libraries.
contributions.text_original:
Dŷch chi'n codi pwynt pwysig dros ben, a does gen i ddim y pwerau i ymyrryd yn y fath fodd, ond yr hyn yr ydw i'n ei wneud ar y funud, trwy'r gwaith dŷn ni'n ei wneud, ydy deall beth yw'r sefyllfa o ran llyfrgelloedd ledled Cymru. Maen nhw'n wasanaeth statudol. Dŷn ni'n gwybod bod yna doriadau wedi bod ledled Cymru. Mae nifer o Aelodau yma wedi ymgyrchu o ran ceisio cadw llyfrgelloedd lleol ar agor, a dwi yn poeni yn fawr ynglŷn â dyfodol ein llyfrgelloedd ni—y dyfodol o ran y buddsoddiad hwnnw.

Mae angen inni ddeall beth ydy'r sefyllfa, a dyna pam, o ran cael gweledigaeth a strategaeth hirdymor a bod yn glir o ran y buddsoddiad hirdymor sydd ei angen, y medraf roi'r sicrwydd i'r Aelod fy mod i'n credu bod llyfrgelloedd yn bwysig, bod y gwaith hwn yn digwydd, ac mi fyddwn ni eisiau gweithio gydag awdurdodau lleol, yn sicr, er mwyn sicrhau bod y gwasanaethau iawn yn ein cymunedau ni a bod yna fynediad i'n llyfrgelloedd ni.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Work in relation to a new culture and sports strategy for Wales is happening at the moment, and heritage and the rich culture of our nation are a central part of that. We have a clear vision in terms of developing Wales to be a cultural and sporting powerhouse. We have committed to realising that.
contributions.text_original: Mae'r gwaith o lunio strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd i Gymru yn digwydd ar y funud, ac mae treftadaeth a diwylliant cyfoethog ein cenedl yn rhan ganolog o hyn. Mae gennym ni weledigaeth glir ynghylch datblygu Cymru i fod yn bwerdy diwylliant a chwaraeon. Rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i wireddu hynny.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
Can I be very clear? I disassociate myself with every single comment made and, no, I do not agree with the Member.

I would suggest that the Member takes the time to speak to people that he represents, who will be horrified and frightened by some of the comments made. I would also ask him to be mindful that our different cultural organisations are governed—our museums, for instance—by a code of ethics, and they are working ethically. And that's what I ask of any institution that receives public funding—to work within the ethics in which they are bound, to be respectful, to be mindful, as we are bound by a Members' code of conduct to do so.
contributions.text_original:

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: A football question. [Laughter.]
contributions.text_original: A football question. [Laughter.]

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: Sporting events such as the UEFA under-19 championships are powerful and important opportunities to inspire young people and to encourage greater participation in sport. We will work with partners, including the Football Association of Wales and the Cymru Football Foundation, to build on the momentum of the tournament by supporting grass-roots football, improving access to facilities and strengthening links between schools, clubs and communities.
contributions.text_original: Mae digwyddiadau chwaraeon fel pencampwriaethau dan-19 UEFA yn gyfleoedd pwerus a phwysig i ysbrydoli pobl ifanc ac annog mwy o gyfranogiad mewn chwaraeon. Mi fyddwn yn gweithio gyda phartneriaid, gan gynnwys Cymdeithas Bêl-droed Cymru a Sefydliad Pêl-droed Cymru, i adeiladu ar y momentwm o'r twrnamaint trwy gefnogi pêl-droed ar lawr gwlad, gwella mynediad at gyfleusterau a chryfhau cysylltiadau rhwng ysgolion, clybiau a chymunedau.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
Thank you to the Member for raising those, and, obviously, we were also in Wrexham together on Saturday. I think that museum will hopefully not just inspire people to visit, but inspire people to be more active, to participate. I think there's much more we can do in this area, and that's why we're committed, as a Government, to be working cross-Government. Myself and the Deputy Minister for public health and prevention have already met. We will meet regularly to see how we embed this work, because it's currently not happening as it should.

I'd be very happy as well to meet with the Member to discuss how we can perhaps take forward some of the work, how it also feeds into our new strategy as well, both in terms of health, but also with the new culture strategy, and embedding those opportunities for everybody to be active, to get outdoors, to be able to participate just for fun. Because not everyone will be at the elite level representing Wales, even though some of us may dream of it. But being able to have fun as well is key there. So, I'd be very happy to take that conversation forward with you.

Because not everyone will be at the elite level representing Wales, even though some of us may dream of it. But being able to have fun as well is key there. So, I'd be very happy to take that conversation forward with you.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english: As a new Minister, I have set about trying to build a constructive relationship with the Welsh Rugby Union, ready to challenge when that's needed, and ready to work with them, whilst also respecting their independence. We engage regularly on shared priorities and the development of the game, including participation, facilities, grass-roots development and major events.
contributions.text_original: Fel Gweinidog newydd, dwi wedi mynd ati i geisio perthynas adeiladol gydag Undeb Rygbi Cymru, yn barod i herio pan fo angen, yn barod i gydweithio hefyd, tra'n parchu ei annibyniaeth. Mi ydym ni'n ymgysylltu'n rheolaidd ynglŷn â blaenoriaethau a rennir a datblygu'r gêm, gan gynnwys cyfranogiad, cyfleusterau, datblygu ar lawr gwlad a digwyddiadau mawr.

contributions.item_title_en: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
contributions.text_english:
Well, as I have emphasised during the session, these are independent issues, and it's through Sport Wales that we fund any body. Certainly, if you do have concerns, I can ask Sport Wales to provide more information to you. I think what is very clear from today's session is that there are a number of questions from Members related to the WRU. I'm very eager to work together with Members in relation to any concerns that you have, and I'm very happy to raise these directly with the Welsh Rugby Union. When I was a sports spokesperson, I was quite prepared to ask questions and challenge as well, and, as a Minister, I'm still prepared to do that.

I'm very pleased that so many of you are worried about the future of the game in Wales with such passion, and, if we can all work together, then I think that this is a good place to start.
contributions.text_original:
Wel, fel dwi wedi pwysleisio yn ystod y sesiwn hwn, mae'r rhain yn faterion annibynnol, a drwy Chwaraeon Cymru rydyn ni'n ariannu unrhyw gorff. Yn sicr, os oes gennych chi bryderon, mi fedraf i ofyn i Chwaraeon Cymru fod yn darparu rhagor o wybodaeth i chi. Dwi'n meddwl yr hyn sydd yn glir iawn o sesiwn heddiw ydy bod yna nifer o gwestiynau gan Aelodau ynglŷn ag Undeb Rygbi Cymru. Dwi'n awyddus iawn i gydweithio efo Aelodau ynglŷn ag unrhyw bryderon sydd gennych chi, a dwi'n hapus iawn i fod yn codi'r rhain yn uniongyrchol efo Undeb Rygbi Cymru. Pan oeddwn i'n llefarydd ar ran chwaraeon, mi oeddwn i'n ddigon parod i ofyn cwestiynau a herio hefyd, ac, fel Gweinidog, dwi'n barod iawn i wneud hynny.

Dwi'n falch iawn bod cymaint ohonoch chi yn pryderu am ddyfodol y gêm yng Nghymru gydag angerdd, ac, os cawn ni weithio gyda'n gilydd, yna dwi'n meddwl bod hwnna'n le da i ddechrau.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Llywydd. You will see that there are a number of statements that have been added to today's agenda. Following a request in the Business Committee today, the First Minister's statement has been extended to 60 minutes rather than the 45 previously stated. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to all Members electronically.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Lywydd. Fe fyddwch chi'n gweld bod yna nifer o ddatganiadau wedi'u hychwanegu at agenda heddiw. Yn dilyn cais yn y Pwyllgor Busnes heddiw, mae datganiad y Prif Weinidog wedi'i ymestyn i 60 munud yn hytrach na'r 45 a nodwyd yn y lle cyntaf. Mae hefyd busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael i'r holl Aelodau yn electronig.

contributions.text_english: May I thank the Member for raising this important issue? I should state that I, for many years, have been involved with constituents in my own constituency in dealing with this issue, and I continue to do that as an individual Member. I'm sure that each and every one of us who saw that documentary, Buried, if they weren't aware of this previously, will have been shocked by the impact that this has had. And certainly, as you heard the First Minister stating earlier, in terms of Michael Sheen too, there will be further discussions happening. But this is a problem that has been known for a while and many people have been campaigning for many years. It is important that we as a Government do tackle and address this issue, and I'm pleased to be able to confirm that it is a priority of ours. We are now developing a pan-Wales strategy to restore post-industrial land, so that communities no longer face those possible risks. And I would ask every Member who has examples in their own constituency to become involved in that work with us.
contributions.text_original: Gaf i ddiolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater pwysig hwn? Mi ddylwn i ddatgan fy mod i, ers blynyddoedd lawer, wedi bod yn ymwneud efo etholwyr yn fy etholaeth i ar y mater hwn, ac yn parhau i wneud hynny fel Aelod unigol. Dwi'n siŵr bod pawb ohonom ni a welodd y rhaglen ddogfen Buried, os nad oeddech chi'n ymwybodol o hyn o'r blaen, wedi cael eich syfrdanu gan effaith hwn. Ac yn sicr, fel y clywsoch chi'r Prif Weinidog yn dweud yn gynharach, o ran Michael Sheen hefyd, mi fydd yna drafodaethau pellach yn digwydd. Ond mae hon yn broblem sydd wedi bod yn wybyddus, a nifer o bobl wedi bod yn ymgyrchu am flynyddoedd lawer. Mae'n bwysig ein bod ni fel Llywodraeth yn mynd i'r afael â hyn, a dwi'n falch o allu cadarnhau ei fod o'n flaenoriaeth i ni. Mi ydyn ni rŵan yn mynd ati i ddatblygu strategaeth ledled Cymru i adfer tir ôl-ddiwydiannol yn raddol, fel nad yw cymunedau bellach yn agored i risgiau posib. Ac mi fyddwn i'n gofyn i bob Aelod sydd efo enghreifftiau yn eu hetholaethau nhw i fod yn rhan o'r gwaith hwnnw efo ni.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising an issue that's very important for many of our constituents and for many Members here. I would like to remind all Members that the Green Paper, 'Shaping the Future of Water Governance in Wales', which responds to recommendations made by the Independent Water Commission, has now, and that consultation, concluded. A summary of responses was published on 14 September, so very recently. We are considering the evidence and the views expressed carefully before making a decision on the next step of reform. Our aim, of course, is to ensure a regulatory framework that complies with the requirements of Wales, strengthens accountability and supports better outcomes for customers, communities and the environment. We will of course update all Senedd Members as that work proceeds.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi pwnc sydd yn bwysig iawn i nifer o'n hetholwyr ni ac i nifer o Aelodau yma. Mi fyddwn i'n hoffi atgoffa'r holl Aelodau bod y Papur Gwyrdd, 'Shaping the Future of Water Governance in Wales', sy'n ymateb i argymhellion a wnaed gan y Comisiwn Dŵr Annibynnol, bellach, a'r ymgynghoriad hwnnw, wedi dod i ben. Mi gyhoeddwyd crynodeb o'r ymatebion ar 14 Medi, felly yn ddiweddar iawn. Rydyn ni'n ystyried y dystiolaeth a'r farn a dderbyniwyd yn ofalus cyn gwneud penderfyniadau ar gam nesaf y diwygio. Ein nod wrth gwrs ydy sicrhau fframwaith rheoleiddio sy'n cyd-fynd â blaenoriaethau Cymru, yn cryfhau atebolrwydd ac yn cefnogi canlyniadau gwell i gwsmeriaid, cymunedau a'r amgylchedd. Mi fyddwn ni wrth gwrs yn diweddaru holl Aelodau'r Senedd hon wrth i'r gwaith hwnnw fynd rhagddo.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much. Evidently, what the Member raised is an issue that is discussed regularly by the Cabinet. This is a priority for all of us as elected Members, I would hope. Certainly, I will make the Cabinet Minister aware of your request. We will of course be updating the Senedd in terms of the work that's proceeding as well.
contributions.text_original: Diolch yn fawr iawn. Yn amlwg, mae'r hyn y mae'r Aelod wedi ei godi yn fater sydd yn cael ei drafod yn gyson gan y Cabinet. Mae hwn yn flaenoriaeth i bawb ohonom ni fel Aelodau etholedig, gobeithio. Yn sicr, mi wnaf i wneud y Gweinidog Cabinet yn ymwybodol o'ch cais chi. Mi fyddwn ni wrth gwrs yn diweddaru'r Senedd o ran y gwaith hwnnw sy'n mynd rhagddo hefyd.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I don't know whether you were in the Chamber to hear the First Minister's response and have had an opportunity to see that there is a statement later this afternoon by the Minister with responsibility for education on the publication of the foundational literacy and numeracy plan. I think that the First Minister's statements were unambiguous about this how we consider these results, and, of course, I would encourage every Member, if there are specific issues within your constituency that are causing you concern, to engage with the Minister for education directly.
contributions.text_original: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Wn i ddim a oeddech chi yn y Siambr ar gyfer clywed ymatebion y Prif Weinidog ac a ydych chi wedi cael cyfle i weld bod yna ddatganiad yn hwyrach y prynhawn yma gan y Gweinidog sydd â chyfrifoldeb dros addysg o ran cyhoeddi'r cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol. Dwi'n credu oedd sylwadau'r Prif Weinidog yn ddiamwys o ran sut rydyn ni'n ystyried y canlyniadau hyn, ac wrth gwrs mi fyddwn i'n annog i unrhyw Aelod, os oes yna bethau penodol o fewn eich etholaeth chi sydd yn creu pryder ichi, gysylltu efo'r Gweinidog dros addysg yn uniongyrchol.

contributions.text_english: Well, may I thank you as a Member for raising this important issue? I'm terribly sorry to hear about that impact on your constituents. We're also aware of what that means in terms of missed appointments, with many people having to wait a long time for such appointments. Certainly, I will make the Minister aware of what you've raised this afternoon. I do hope that, if you do have specific examples too, that you raise those with the health board directly, and certainly with the Minister too. So I will feed that back to him following this session.
contributions.text_original: Wel, gaf i ddiolch ichi fel Aelod am godi'r mater pwysig hwn? Mae'n ddrwg calon gen i glywed am yr effaith hynny ar etholwyr. Rydyn ni hefyd yn gwybod beth mae hynny'n ei olygu o ran apwyntiadau wedi eu methu, efo nifer o bobl yn gorfod aros amser maith am apwyntiadau o'r fath. Yn sicr mi wnaf i'r Gweinidog yn ymwybodol o'r hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi heddiw. Dwi'n gobeithio, os oes gennych chi esiamplau penodol hefyd, eich bod chi'n codi'r rheini efo'r bwrdd iechyd yn uniongyrchol, ac yn sicr efo'r Gweinidog hefyd. Felly, mi fyddaf i'n bwydo hynny nôl iddo fo yn dilyn y sesiwn hon.

contributions.text_english: Well, thank you for raising this. The fact that you're the second Member to do so does demonstrate how much concern there is. A local authority survey held by NRW noted in 2015 that there were over 9,000 possible sites that need further investigation. Although not every one of those sites poses a risk to human health or the environment, this figure does show the scale of the problem facing regulators in Wales. As you heard earlier, tackling contaminated land is a key priority of this Government, and we will be developing a pan-Wales strategy to restore post-industrial land so that communities aren't facing possible risks. We, as I also reached out to Llŷr Powell, would ask you and every other Member that is concerned about this issue to work with us as a Government.
contributions.text_original: Wel, diolch ichi am godi hyn. Mae'r ffaith mai chi yw'r ail Aelod i godi hwn yn dangos faint o bryder sydd. Mae'n ffaith bod arolwg awdurdodau lleol a gynhaliwyd gan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru wedi nodi yn 2015 fod mwy na 9,000 o safleoedd posib sydd angen eu hymchwilio ymhellach. Er na fydd pob un o'r safleoedd hyn yn peri risg i iechyd pobl neu'r amgylchedd, mae'r ffigur hwn yn dangos maint y broblem sy'n wynebu rheoleiddwyr yng Nghymru. Fel y clywsoch chi'n gynharach, mae mynd i'r afael â thir halogedig yn flaenoriaeth allweddol i'r Llywodraeth hon, ac mi fyddwn ni'n mynd ati i ddatblygu strategaeth ledled Cymru i adfer tir ôl-ddiwydiannol fel nad yw cymunedau yn agored i risgiau posibl. Mi fyddwn ni hefyd, fel y gwnes i ymestyn allan i Llŷr Powell yn gynharach, yn gofyn ichi a phob Aelod arall sydd yn pryderu am hyn i gydweithio efo ni fel Llywodraeth.

contributions.text_english: The Member will have heard previous statements by the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy. As the work proceeds, there will, of course, be further updates to the Senedd and an opportunity for Members to scrutinise and provide further input on the matter.
contributions.text_original: Mi fydd yr Aelod wedi clywed datganiadau blaenorol gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni. Wrth i'r gwaith fynd rhagddo, wrth gwrs, mi fydd yna ddiweddariadau i'r Senedd a chyfle i Aelodau graffu a rhoi mewnbwn pellach.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this issue. It's important to note that the health board hasn't made any decision on its clinical services plan. Can I be very clear that every death on our roads is a tragedy, and road safety remains a priority for this Government? I also would think that the Member would not wish to mislead the public, because the data does show that collisions were 22 per cent lower than in 2022, the most recent full calendar year before the change in default speed limits was implemented. There was a 2 per cent increase in 2024, but may I just emphasise this is the second lowest annual number recorded in Wales, with the lowest being in 2024?

We will always keep every policy under review. That is good government. But I think we also need to look at the statistics and be honest with people in terms of really understanding the impact of a policy over a longer term, which was always the case with this. But I would ask the Member to reflect on the actual data and what it stands for, and be careful in how we present that data.

Thank you very much to the Member for raising that important issue. As with the previous question, clearly, I am answering as Trefnydd today, but it is relevant in terms of the debate later today on the supplementary budget, because, clearly, there is £2 million allocated in that supplementary budget to start to address the challenges facing schools, and a percentage of that funding will be for travel costs.

In addition to that, there is a Government commitment to carry out an analysis of all of the sports assets, including swimming pools, that we have across Wales to truly understand (1) what's been lost and (2) what is at risk of being lost, because many of our swimming pools are very old, in order to put a long-term plan into place. Everyone should have access to swimming lessons. Everyone in Wales should have access to swimming pools. But, unfortunately, there have been cuts, and that's why this work must proceed. I would encourage any Member here today who is passionate, as am I and as is my party, about ensuring that every child in primary school in Wales has a right to access swimming lessons free of charge, in order to learn such an important skill, to support the supplementary budget today.

Well, thank you for raising that. Obviously, many Members here will have been sharing those warnings about not walking dogs or taking care of animals and livestock during the extreme weather, and greyhounds are no exception.

The welfare of greyhounds must be a primary consideration whenever racing takes place, including during periods of hot weather. We know the high temperatures can present additional welfare risks for racing dogs, which is why it is important that track operators carefully assess local conditions and implement appropriate measures to protect animal welfare. Those responsible for racing greyhounds also have a duty to monitor dogs closely, ensuring access to shade and water, and, as a Government, we would expect any decisions relating to racing in hot weather to be informed by veterinary—oh, sorry—veterinary advice—veterinary, sorry, advice; you can tell I usually say that word in Welsh—and welfare considerations for the specific circumstances at the track.

contributions.text_english: The Member will be aware that there is an offer on the table, and a subsequent offer made since the unions made contact, that is more than what was on the table had Labour been re-elected to lead this Welsh Government. So, very clearly, there is now a pathway this afternoon for yourselves, ourselves, to join forces and unlock the substantial additional funding for ALN this year and in future years. That is within our power today: £40 million for ALN today; £40 million the following year; £40 million—[Interruption.] More than the £9 million you had on the table. So, we can play politics or we can think of those children with additional learning needs. We can work together for those children with additional learning needs and put in place a plan that is workable, deliverable and meaningful. That is your choice today, and I really hope that you make the right choice.

I thank the Member for raising this very important issue. I'm sure that we've all been shocked to see the pictures on the television. For those residents, it's difficult to imagine the severe damage. I share the comments made by the Member, in terms of paying tribute not only to the firefighters, but everyone who was part of the response in north Wales, who worked together to keep people and communities safe.

Significant progress has been made in terms of bringing the number of wildfires under control. As the Member mentioned, the general situation has improved, but we do know that this, unfortunately, is one of the effects of climate change now. It's an issue that we as a Government are giving attention to, deservedly, and we're looking across Government, as you heard from the First Minister earlier today. With the temperatures we're experiencing in Wales now, we need to be completely united, I think, as a Senedd, in terms of how we're going to respond to the increasing likelihood of wildfires. The impact that this has, as you said, in terms of health is significant, and in terms of wildlife and nature is significant. We, therefore, have to ensure that that plan is in place. And if there is specific support that residents have engaged with the Member about that you want to engage with us as a Government about, I'd encourage you to engage with the relevant Government Ministers.

Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater eithriadol o bwysig. Dwi'n siŵr ein bod ni i gyd wedi'n brawychu o weld y lluniau ar y teledu. I'r trigolion hynny, mae'n anodd dychmygu’r niwed difrifol. Wrth gwrs, dwi'n rhannu'r sylwadau a wnaed gan yr Aelod, o ran talu teyrnged nid yn unig i'r diffoddwyr tân, ond i bawb fu'n rhan o'r ymateb yng ngogledd Cymru, sydd wedi gweithio ar y cyd i gadw pobl a chymunedau'n ddiogel.

Mi wnaed cynnydd sylweddol o ran dod â nifer y tanau gwyllt o dan reolaeth. Fel roedd yr Aelod yn sôn, mae'r sefyllfa'n gyffredinol wedi gwella'n sylweddol, ond rydyn ni'n gwybod bod hyn, yn anffodus, yn un o effeithiau newid hinsawdd rŵan. Mae o'n fater rydyn ni fel Llywodraeth yn rhoi sylw haeddiannol iddo fo, yn edrych yn draws lywodraethol, fel y clywsoch chi gan y Prif Weinidog yn gynharach heddiw. Gyda'r tymheredd rydyn ni'n ei brofi yng Nghymru erbyn hyn, mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn gyfan gwbl unedig, dwi'n credu, fel Senedd ynglŷn â sut rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn ymateb i'r tebygolrwydd cynyddol o danau gwyllt. Mae'r effaith y mae hyn yn ei gael, fel oeddech chi'n sôn, ar iechyd yn aruthrol, ac o ran bywyd gwyllt a natur yn aruthrol. Mae'n rhaid i ni, felly, sicrhau bod y cynllun hwnnw'n ei le. Ac os oes yna gymorth penodol y mae trigolion wedi bod yn ymgysylltu efo'r Aelod amdano fo yr ydych chi eisiau ymgysylltu efo ni fel Llywodraeth amdano, byddwn i'n eich annog chi i wneud cysylltiad efo'r Aelodau Llywodraeth perthnasol.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much for raising an issue of real importance, something I know that many in this Senedd are concerned about and are passionate about. I'm not going to be attempting to make any statements before we hear from the First Minister later this afternoon, but, certainly, I hope that that unambiguous commitment on the importance of that has been made clear by me this afternoon.

Yn sicr, mi oedd yna ymrwymiad cadarn ym maniffesto Plaid Cymru—ac mae'r ymrwymiad cadarn hwnnw yn parhau o fewn Plaid Cymru—i sicrhau bod yr hawl i brynu cymunedol yn dod yn ddeddfwriaeth. Dwi ddim yn mynd i fod yn ceisio gwneud unrhyw ddatganiadau cyn inni glywed gan y Prif Weinidog yn hwyrach y prynhawn yma, ond, yn sicr, gobeithio bod yr ymrwymiad diamwys hwnnw o ran pwysigrwydd hyn wedi'i wneud gen i y prynhawn yma.

I thank the Member for that. Evidently, the First Minister was asked about this issue earlier today. We've also had the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution. What I can state very clearly to every Member here is that we, as Ministers, started that scrutiny work on day one, questioning every budget line as soon as we had access to the whole range of information. That analysis continues. We have further work to do over the summer, but the difference that you have in this Government is that commitment to work across portfolios to ensure that every single pound gives the people of Wales the greatest possible benefit. It's not about safeguarding our own budgets so that one thing can be delivered, but looking at, 'How can this pound be used in order to do a variety of things?' That's the work that's proceeding. 

We are also looking strategically and on a long-term basis. We're not just looking at those things that generate easy headlines, but how we're going to improve things fundamentally. And that's why, with additional learning needs, we have a three-year commitment that this Senedd could vote for today. That's why we're going at it, with the NHS, not just to throw money at it but to come up with long-term, transformative plans that are going to make a genuine difference. The problem in the past, as we've seen, was that a little money was given but there was no getting to the root of the problem. That's the difference with this Government, and we're being totally transparent with everyone about that.

Diolch i'r Aelod am hynny. Yn amlwg, mi gafodd y Prif Weinidog ei holi ar y mater hwn yn gynharach heddiw. Mi ydyn ni hefyd wedi cael y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad. Yr hyn y medraf i ei ddweud yn gyfan gwbl glir wrth bob Aelod yma ydy ein bod ni, fel Gweinidogion, wedi dechrau'r gwaith craffu hwnnw ar ddiwrnod un, yn cwestiynu pob llinell yn ein cyllidebau ni y funud roedd gennym ni fynediad at yr holl ystod yna o wybodaeth. Mae'r dadansoddi hwnnw yn parhau. Mae gennym ni waith pellach i'w wneud dros yr haf, ond y gwahaniaeth sydd gennych chi yn y Llywodraeth hon ydy'r ymrwymiad i weithio ar draws portffolios i sicrhau bod pob punt posib yn cael y budd mwyaf i bobl Cymru. Dydy o ddim ynglŷn â diogelu ein cyllidebau ni fel bod un peth yn gallu cael ei gyflawni, ond edrych, 'Sut mae'r bunt yma yn gallu cael ei defnyddio er mwyn gwneud amryw o bethau amrywiol?' Dyna'r gwaith sy'n mynd rhagddo.

Hefyd, rydym yn edrych yn strategol ac yn hirdymor. Dydyn ni ddim yn edrych ar y pethau sy'n mynd i greu headlines yn hawdd, ond yn edrych ar sut ydyn ni'n mynd i wella pethau'n sylfaenol. Dyna pam, efo anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, mae yna ymrwymiad tair blynedd y gall y Senedd hon fod yn pleidleisio o'i blaid heddiw. Dyna pam ein bod ni'n mynd ati, efo'r gwasanaeth iechyd, nid i daflu arian ato ond i ddod i fyny efo chynlluniau hirdymor, trawsnewidiol sy'n mynd i wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol. Y drwg yn y gorffennol, fel rydyn ni wedi ei weld, oedd rhoi bach o arian ond peidio mynd at wraidd y broblem. Dyna'r newid efo'r Llywodraeth hon, ac rydyn ni'n gyfan gwbl dryloyw efo pawb ohonoch chi ynglŷn â hynny.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising that issue. As you heard, I think, in my response to a Member earlier, that's exactly why we are now seeking to understand what has been lost and what investment is required, so that we can either reopen swimming pools or ensure that swimming pools that are at risk of closure can be kept open. We have to have a national plan. Unfortunately, there has been significant underinvestment in swimming pools. This is a huge problem here in Wales. It's something that we are looking at as part of our new swimming programme. Because it's one thing to give swimming lessons, but if you don't have the swimming pools available, then provision will be difficult. So, the commitment that we have is to look across Wales, including Pontardawe, to see what the need is. Then Sport Wales will assess the investment required. But the one thing I would say to Members is that the amount of capital money being put into swimming pools at the moment is not going to be able to meet the requirements across Wales. So, we do have to look at diverse models and how we can ensure that swimming pools can remain open in our communities for the benefit of people of all ages, as the Member said at the beginning of her question.

contributions.text_english: I thank the Member for raising this important issue. Clearly, in terms of empowering communities, that's something that this Government has committed to. We certainly believe that we need to look again at processes in terms of planning and community engagement in order to ensure that the voice of local residents and local people is heard. It was one of the reasons why a number of us campaigned when we were in the opposition parties in terms of a number of the measures that are in our manifesto and our programme for government. The voice of communities is important and it's very difficult when they don't have the kind of resources that they need to proceed with the kinds of studies that you mentioned when companies, sometimes international ones, have so much money that can support them to challenge things against the community.

Mi oedd o'n un o'r rhesymau pam roedd nifer ohonom ni wedi ymgyrchu pan oeddem ni yn y gwrthbleidiau o ran nifer o'r mesurau sydd rŵan yn ein maniffesto ni ac sydd yn ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni. I would ask—[Interruption.] I would ask the Member to reflect—[Interruption.] I do apologise—does the Member want to hear the response? Is it okay for me to respond? Thank you. 

What I would say is that the draft budget has been fully published. It's there for scrutiny. Clearly, there is a committee established to directly scrutinise this issue. We're entirely transparent. This is how we want to govern. And that change can be seen in the way that we want to work on a cross-party basis and be open. We are serious about addressing these deficiencies that we have, unfortunately, inherited. That is on the record; it is transparent. And, of course, the Cabinet Minister for Finance will be scrutinised specifically on this by the Finance Committee.
